title: Simultaneous call capacity: check the complete path
description: Check concurrent calls across your carrier, phone system and answering provider. Separate active conversations, ringing patterns and burst limits.
lead: Several phones ringing for one caller is different from handling several callers at once.
intro: For a home-service office, simultaneous call capacity means the number of separate calls a particular setup can sustain at the same time. It is not the number of extensions that ring for one caller, and it is not a monthly allowance of answering minutes. Trace the entire path before relying on a capacity claim: the published number, carrier, phone system, answering destination and any transfer back to your office.

overviewTable.caption: Capacity acceptance matrix: obtain the limit and observed outcome for each leg
rows: How many overlapping inbound calls does this exact service admit?
Product, account scope and carrier confirmation
Which channel, session, license or account limit applies?
Does a separate simultaneous caller connect, wait, overflow or receive busy?
Provider terms and a controlled observation
Can another call reach the receiving endpoint while it is occupied?
Is admission limited by call starts per second as well as active calls?
Direction-specific rate limit and allowed test plan
What is the next caller's final path?
Queue, rejection or fallback record with owner

sections.title: Keep three different quantities separate
paragraphs: Concurrent calls are calls overlapping in time. Simultaneous ringing describes attempts to reach several destinations for a single caller. Calls per second, often called CPS, describes how quickly new calls can start or be admitted in a specified direction. A system can have room for ongoing conversations while applying a separate limit to new call attempts.

Twilio's Elastic SIP Trunking documentation illustrates the distinction: it lists concurrent calls separately from origination and termination CPS. Its stated allowances depend on carrier support, and it warns that new accounts without an approved Business Profile have limited concurrency. These are Twilio SIP trunking terms, not a Revo limit or proof that an entire business call path is unlimited.

sources.label: Twilio Elastic SIP Trunking scale and account qualifications; reviewed October 22, 2026

sections.title: Locate the restriction instead of multiplying plan minutes
paragraphs: Draw one row for each service in the route. Ask whether its limit applies per number, account, trunk, licensed user or answering team. Record direction as well: an inbound call and a transfer that creates an outbound leg may face different controls. If the provider uses channels or sessions, ask how those units relate to a held or transferred call in your configuration.

A monthly minute allowance describes billed usage, not the number of simultaneous conversations your business can receive. Likewise, several purchased numbers do not prove independent capacity if they share an account restriction. Leave an undocumented limit unresolved in the matrix instead of assuming it is absent.
items: Identify the actual carrier and product behind the advertised number.
Record shared limits as shared; do not allocate the same capacity independently to each branch.
Ask what happens to a caller who arrives while all permitted capacity is occupied.

sections.title: Agree a small acceptance sequence before making test calls
paragraphs: Choose the overlap your office needs from its own demand records and obtain the providers' permission for the test method. Use consenting participants, known test numbers and a staff-approved window. Do not flood the production number or discover a limit by repeatedly increasing traffic without authorization.

Keep the first test conversation connected, then place a separate authorized call to the published number. Record whether it connects independently, waits, reaches a fallback or fails. Repeat only up to the agreed scope. Where transfers are part of the required flow, include that leg in the approved test and record whether it changes the experience of another caller. A successful test establishes an observation at that load and time, not an unlimited-capacity guarantee.
items: Retain call IDs or timestamps, direction, overlap and outcome for each test.
Record active calls separately from held calls and ringing attempts.
Have the provider confirm whether a separate burst-rate test is necessary and supported.

sections.title: Accept the overflow outcome as part of capacity
paragraphs: A capacity plan needs an agreed result for the next caller, not only a successful result below the limit. Specify whether that caller waits, hears an announcement, reaches another destination or is rejected. Identify who monitors unanswered requests and who can change the account's capacity when requirements change.

Recheck the matrix after changing the carrier, account, phone system, transfer destination or branch structure. Keep a provider's published limit, the account's configured limit and your observed acceptance result in separate fields. None alone establishes the others. Do not infer Revo concurrency, burst capacity or a service-level guarantee from this guide.

faqs.q: Does ringing five phones mean we can answer five simultaneous callers?
faqs.a: No. Five destinations can be ringing for one call. Ask separately how many distinct overlapping calls the full setup can admit and handle.

faqs.q: Do more monthly minutes increase simultaneous capacity?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The minute allowance and concurrency limit measure different things. Obtain the account-specific capacity rule instead of deriving it from a usage plan.

faqs.q: Can an unlimited concurrency statement still have qualifications?
faqs.a: Yes. Twilio's SIP trunking documentation, for example, distinguishes CPS and concurrency and states carrier and new-account qualifications. Read the scope and check every other service in the route.

takeaway: Document concurrent capacity, arrival-rate limits and the overflow outcome across the full route, then verify the agreed operating requirement with an authorized test.

title: Appointment waitlist: fill an opening without double booking
description: Manage an appointment waitlist with customer permission, service-fit checks, offer deadlines and a final calendar check before confirming an open slot.
lead: Keep a request for an opening separate from a confirmed visit.
intro: A customer wants an earlier service appointment, but the calendar has no suitable opening. A waitlist records permission to contact that customer if a compatible slot becomes available. It does not reserve a visit, establish an arrival time or replace the appointment already on the calendar.

sections.title: Choose a managed list or a verified scheduling feature.
paragraphs: A small office can maintain a controlled list or use an external request form, with one person responsible for reviewing new entries. A form submission alone does not check the service area, match a technician or reserve time. Document who turns a submitted request into a reviewed entry.

YouCanBookMe’s official help article, reviewed October 22, 2026, says it does not provide a waitlist after a booking page becomes fully booked. It suggests linking a web document or Google Form so customers can join a list the business manages. That workaround is not automatic slot matching or automatic promotion into an appointment.

If you buy another scheduling product with waitlist functions, verify its matching rules, holds and confirmation behavior separately. This guide describes an office process; it does not establish a native Revo waitlist feature or an integration with any named scheduler.
items: Choose the system of record and limit access to the staff who need it.
Assign an owner and a backup for reviewing requests and outstanding offers.
State plainly on the form that joining does not guarantee an opening.

sections.title: Collect permission and the conditions that make a slot useful.
paragraphs: Ask whether the customer wants contact about an earlier opening, which approved contact method to use and when the request should expire. Record the response rather than assuming that an ordinary booking permits every kind of waitlist contact. Provide a way to withdraw the request.

Check the work type, service location, required appointment duration and acceptable days or time windows against your office’s scheduling rules. A spare hour is not a suitable opening when the work requires a longer visit or a technician who will be elsewhere. Keep uncertain requests for staff review rather than promising a fit.

For a customer who already has a later appointment, link the waitlist entry to that booking. Keep it in place unless the customer accepts a replacement and the office completes the change. For a customer without a booking, say that the waitlist is still only a request.
items: Entry fields: internal request ID, contact permission and method, work type, service area, availability windows and expiry date.
Priority rule: a declared order among compatible requests, with any approved exception documented.
Separate urgent or safety-related concerns from an ordinary earlier-appointment request; use the business’s established response process.

sections.title: Offer one compatible slot through a controlled process.
paragraphs: When an opening appears, recheck the actual calendar, technician availability, travel constraints and service fit. Select the next compatible entry under the declared priority rule. An older request for a different day need not be a match for this particular slot; record the reason it was skipped.

Send a specific offer through the agreed channel: proposed date and time or arrival window, what visit it covers, how to accept and the response deadline with time zone. State whether the slot is being held and until when. If the scheduler cannot hold it, explain that availability must be rechecked before confirmation.

Use one active offer per slot unless your scheduling system has a verified method to prevent conflicting acceptances. A customer’s acceptance starts the final booking check; it is not proof that the calendar was updated. If the deadline passes or the customer declines, close that offer before moving to the next person. For delivery failures or unclear replies, use the agreed alternative contact method or staff review rather than assuming acceptance.
items: Offer record: slot, selected request, sent time, deadline, hold status and staff owner.
Before contacting the next entry, resolve any current hold or outstanding acceptance.
Do not offer the same opening independently from several staff inboxes.

sections.title: Confirm the calendar change and close the loop.
paragraphs: After acceptance, the office checks availability again and records the appointment in the authoritative schedule. Only then send the confirmation. If replacing an existing appointment, complete the change as one controlled workflow and verify that the customer has the intended booking rather than two conflicting appointments.

If the slot is no longer available, explain the outcome and ask whether the customer wants to remain on the list. Keep an unanswered offer, an expired offer and a declined offer as different statuses. Remove or close entries when the customer withdraws, the request expires or a suitable appointment is confirmed.

Review open entries and offers at a defined office interval. The useful control is reconciliation: every active offer has an owner, every confirmed waitlist placement has a calendar record, and expired requests are no longer contacted as though they were current.
items: Check the customer, work, location and appointment details before confirmation.
Record the confirmation reference and close or update the linked waitlist entry.
Review stale requests, undelivered offers and any acceptance awaiting a calendar decision.

overviewTable.caption: Suggested office statuses — adapt these to your actual scheduling system
rows: Customer asked to join; fit and permission may still need review
Check eligibility, availability preferences and contact permission
Reviewed entry awaiting a compatible opening
Apply the declared priority rule when a matching slot appears
A particular opening was offered with a stated deadline
Track owner, hold status, response and expiry; avoid conflicting offers
This offer ended without a completed booking
Release any hold; close the offer before selecting another request
Customer agreed to the proposed slot
Recheck the schedule; do not call it confirmed yet
The office recorded the appointment and sent confirmation
Link the schedule record; resolve any replaced appointment and close the entry
Withdrawn, expired or no longer needed
Stop using the entry for new offers

faqs.q: Does joining an appointment waitlist reserve a time?
faqs.a: No. It records a request for a compatible opening. An offer, customer acceptance and the office’s completed calendar confirmation are separate steps.

faqs.q: Does YouCanBookMe automatically fill a cancelled appointment from a waitlist?
faqs.a: The official help article reviewed October 22, 2026 describes linking to an external document or form for a list the business manages. It does not establish automatic matching or booking from that list.

faqs.q: Should I cancel a customer’s later appointment when they join?
faqs.a: Joining alone is not an accepted replacement. Keep the existing appointment until the customer accepts a suitable offer and the office completes and confirms the intended schedule change.

takeaway: Obtain permission, match the opening and confirm the schedule before promising a visit.

title: Call and text forwarding: verify each channel
description: Check voice routing, incoming SMS, email copies and reply identity separately before moving or forwarding a home-service business number.
lead: Verify where calls and texts go before relying on a forwarded number.
intro: A business number can receive a voice call and a text message through different configurations. Before forwarding or moving the number, map the destination for each channel and the method used to reply. A working forwarded call does not establish that customer texts arrive at the same phone, or that a reply uses the business number.

sections.title: Specify the channel and the action you need.
paragraphs: For each public number, record the current provider, the proposed change and the required result. Distinguish keeping the number with its current provider and forwarding voice calls from transferring the number to another provider. Ask the providers which voice and messaging arrangements the exact number can use before scheduling a change.

Use precise language in a quote: receiving an SMS in an app, receiving an email copy and relaying an SMS to another mobile number are different requirements. If staff must reply from the business number, ask which approved app or service sends that reply. Do not infer the answer from a feature called “text forwarding.”
items: Identify whether the number is local or toll-free.
List required voice, SMS and any picture-message behavior separately.

sections.title: Use the NumberBarn example to separate forwarding from notification.
paragraphs: NumberBarn’s features page describes forwarding calls to another phone number. Its Text Messaging Overview, updated October 7, 2026, separately describes an email notification that copies incoming texts to up to two email addresses. The email-setting instructions identify the receiving email addresses. These documents demonstrate separate channel controls; an email copy is not documentation of SMS relay to another mobile number or of replying by email.

The use restriction matters for a business. NumberBarn describes its own messaging as personal P2P messaging. Its business-messaging instructions instead point to String, with separate eligibility and registration requirements. The example therefore explains a configuration distinction; it is not a recommendation to use personal messaging for customer communications.

NumberBarn business messaging with String — reviewed October 22, 2026

sections.title: Get compatibility answers before a migration.
paragraphs: Ask the proposed provider to confirm support for this exact number and business use, where incoming messages will be stored, what happens to the current messaging setup and which product staff will use afterward. Record any activation or registration dependency separately from the voice-routing change. Leave an unanswered requirement unresolved rather than marking the number ready.

Prepare a small acceptance record for both providers: the number, each requested change, the responsible account administrator and the order in which changes are expected. Ask what can be reversed and what requires support. Decide how the office will notice a failed channel during the transition instead of treating a successful voice test as completion.
items: Confirm local or toll-free support with the proposed messaging provider.
Record the agreed handling of existing messages and access before changing service.

sections.title: Test delivery and return identity independently.
paragraphs: Use consenting testers and clearly labeled test messages. After the approved configuration change, place a voice call to the public number, send a new text to that same number and check the expected receiving system. If an email copy is configured, check that copy separately. Then send a reply through the approved business-messaging tool and record the number the tester sees.

Keep the observations by channel: original number dialed or texted, destination reached, reply method and displayed return number. A delivered email cannot establish that a mobile SMS relay works. A reply from an employee’s personal number cannot establish business-number reply support. If a required result fails, pause acceptance of that channel and use the documented provider escalation or reversal process.
items: Use the same public number in each acceptance test.
Confirm the normal voice greeting still works after a messaging change.

faqs.q: Does forwarding voice calls also forward customer texts?
faqs.a: Verify messaging separately for the exact number and service. Voice-call delivery does not establish where incoming SMS is received or how staff can reply.

faqs.q: Is an emailed copy of a text the same as SMS forwarding to a mobile?
faqs.a: No. The receiving channel is email. A copy does not establish delivery as an SMS to another number, or an ability to send a business-number reply from that email.

faqs.q: Can NumberBarn’s personal texting example be used as evidence of business SMS support?
faqs.a: No. Its documented personal P2P messaging and its separate business-messaging route have different requirements. Confirm the applicable business product and number eligibility directly.

faqs.q: What should we check after moving messaging to another service?
faqs.a: Test a new incoming text, its destination and an approved business-number reply. Also repeat a voice call to confirm that the required voice route still works.

takeaway: Accept a number change only after voice delivery, incoming messaging and the required reply identity have each passed their own test.

title: Vonage virtual receptionist setup: menus and exceptions
description: Set up a Vonage virtual receptionist with the right administrator, no-input action and schedule priority, then test the actual caller path.
lead: Configure the menu, its schedule and the caller who presses nothing.
intro: Vonage calls this feature a Virtual Receptionist: an automated menu that routes calls using configured schedules. This guide concerns that menu system, not a conversational AI service that collects a home-service request. The setup below combines documented controls with a proposed acceptance test for an office administrator.

sections.title: Create the receptionist and save its general settings.
paragraphs: An authorized Super User or Account Administrator uses the Admin Portal, not the mobile app. In Virtual Receptionist, select Add New. Complete General Settings: name, extension, applicable location, associated telephone number and No Caller Input Handling; click Save.

Before editing an existing setup, record which public business number should reach this menu and how it currently behaves. Have the authorized administrator confirm the selected account and receptionist. Do not create a second menu merely because an employee cannot find the first one in the mobile app.

sources.label: Vonage Virtual Receptionist: access and general settings — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Choose the no-input result before polishing the greeting.
paragraphs: For no input, set the wait, repeats and final action. Outside-line forwarding is documented at $0.03/minute, with international rates applicable.

For a proposed repair-office menu, write the action beside each announced key. Then write the outcome for a caller who makes no selection. Read the recording against that map: if it promises that the office will receive a message, the configured result must actually reach the intended mailbox. A greeting alone does not create that delivery path.

sources.label: Vonage no-input and call-flow controls — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Add the schedule and call flow, then finish and save.
paragraphs: Under Schedules and Call Flows, select Add New. Name the schedule; choose All Day or Specify Hours and Dates, recurrence and ending. Select Next or Call Flow. Apply an available shared flow, or name a new flow, choose Live Operator settings, routing behavior and greeting. Click Done. If applicable, edit After Hours Schedule through its three-dot menu and configure that flow; click Save. Controls verified October 23, 2026 against the article updated April 15, 2026.

Use one concrete exception to check the design. Suppose an office closes for a team meeting while its normal weekday hours remain open. Identify the exception schedule, its intended end and the flow it should select. If an operator-first attempt is used, observe whether the menu resumes when that person does not answer. These are proposed tests, not evidence that any particular account is already configured.
items: General settings alone leave an incomplete receptionist inactive.
Always in Front overrides other schedules.
Keep Try Live Operator First shorter than voicemail interception.

sources.label: Vonage schedules and operator-first behavior — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Accept the changed route with a short call record.
paragraphs: Choose a provider-supported test method and an agreed window. With consenting test callers, call the associated business number and record the expected schedule, greeting, key selected and final endpoint. Include a call with no input and an unanswered operator-first attempt if that option is enabled.

Have the administrator compare the result with the saved design before directing customer traffic to a new route. Preserve the previous settings and the account-specific restoration instructions. After an exception ends, confirm that the normal flow resumes and that no temporary announcement remains in the caller path.
items: Record the receptionist and schedule names in the test notes.
Treat an unanswered destination separately from a menu selection that worked.

faqs.q: Can an employee edit the Virtual Receptionist from the Vonage mobile app?
faqs.a: Use the portal workflow above with the authorized account administrator; this guide does not provide mobile editing instructions.

faqs.q: Does the name Virtual Receptionist mean it collects service requests conversationally?
faqs.a: This documented feature is an automated menu and routing system. A separate service’s ability to collect a request should be evaluated separately.

faqs.q: Why test a caller who presses nothing?
faqs.a: That caller follows the configured no-input path. Testing only a successful menu selection leaves that outcome unchecked.

takeaway: Accept the Vonage setup when the called number, no-input action, schedule exception and operator-first outcome match the approved design.

title: 8x8 virtual receptionist: Auto Attendant or Power Keys?
description: Distinguish 8x8 Auto Attendant from legacy Power Keys, then check destinations, site, time zone and holiday rules for the current menu setup.
lead: Find the right administration guide before changing the caller menu.
intro: The phrase 8x8 virtual receptionist has more than one documented meaning. Current Auto Attendant documentation uses it for a caller menu; older Account Manager documentation says Power Keys was formerly called Virtual Receptionist. This guide separates those meanings, then covers the current Auto Attendant menu and schedule. It is not a guide to conversational AI intake.

sections.title: Identify a caller menu or an operator’s phone keys.
paragraphs: The older Power Keys guide describes an add-on for handling calls and monitoring extensions through phone line keys, including line appearances, busy lamp fields and speed dials. Its configuration belongs to Account Manager and enabled extensions. That is different from the current Auto Attendant guide, which describes callers choosing a route from a menu.

If the task concerns buttons on a receptionist’s desk phone, stop before following the menu procedure below and identify the account product and applicable Power Keys documentation. The older guide is evidence of terminology, not confirmation that a particular device, add-on or migration path remains available today. If the task concerns the greeting and keypad choices callers hear, proceed with the current Auto Attendant scope.

sources.label: 8x8 older Account Manager Power Keys terminology — reviewed October 23, 2026
8x8 current Auto Attendant scope — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Prepare the destinations and select the correct Site.
paragraphs: The setup guide, updated September 11, 2026, lists user profiles, Ring Groups, Call Queues and extension forwarding rules as prerequisites where required. Creation starts in Admin Console under Auto Attendants. A Site must be selected before menu rules can be created.

For the office’s proposed menu, identify the exact destination object for each key before recording the prompt. For example, an existing-customer choice could point to an agreed office destination while new inquiries use another approved path. Record the selected object name and intended recipient so an administrator can distinguish a similarly named object at another site. This example does not establish how an existing account is configured.

sources.label: 8x8 Auto Attendant prerequisites and Site requirement — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Set the time zone, then resolve the holiday exception.
paragraphs: The Auto Attendant profile includes its time zone, and the weekly hours follow that selection. The separate holiday guide says holiday schedules override standard business hours on the selected dates. Holiday exceptions can specify open or closed status; holiday handling can reuse the weekday open menu or define a custom menu.

Before saving a closure, write the date, intended local hours and destination beside the greeting. Consider a service office open for limited hours on a normally full workday: the exception must identify both the limited open period and the closed result. Compare the Holiday Open Hours and Holiday Closed Hours menus instead of assuming that changing the recording changes the route. Keep the announcement consistent with actual office coverage.

sources.label: 8x8 Auto Attendant time-zone setting — reviewed October 23, 2026
8x8 holiday precedence and call-handling menus — reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Test the schedule result through the public number.
paragraphs: Arrange a supported test method and window with the authorized administrator; use consenting test callers. For each case in the worksheet, record the business number called, test time and time zone, active menu, key selection and destination reached. A successful call to a Ring Group directly does not check whether the public number selected the correct holiday menu.

Keep the previous configuration and its approved restoration procedure available. After the exception has ended, confirm that the normal weekday behavior returns. If the greeting is correct but the recipient is wrong, investigate the menu action and destination object separately. If the recipient is correct but the wrong hours apply, review the time zone and exception date before editing destinations.

Preserve the test record with the Site and Auto Attendant names.

faqs.q: Does 8x8 virtual receptionist always mean Auto Attendant?
faqs.a: No. The older Power Keys documentation uses Virtual Receptionist as a former name for a phone-key call-handling add-on. Identify the account product and the task before selecting instructions.

faqs.q: Does this guide establish which phones support Power Keys today?
faqs.a: No. The older page explains the terminology. Verify current device, account and add-on compatibility with 8x8 before planning a Power Keys configuration.

faqs.q: Why can I not create the Auto Attendant menu rules?
faqs.a: The cited current setup guide requires a Site to be selected before menu rules can be created. Have the authorized administrator check that field and the intended account configuration.

faqs.q: Will normal weekly hours take priority on a configured holiday?
faqs.a: The holiday guide says holiday schedules override standard business hours on the selected dates. Verify the date, time zone and the holiday open and closed handling before relying on it.

title: Reception247: plans, rounded minutes and contractor intake
description: Review Reception247 Answer Pro and Total Assistant Pro plans, per-call minute rounding, transfer fees and published contractor scheduling support.
lead: Choose the task first, then reconcile rounded minutes and transfers.
intro: Reception247 publishes two US plan families with different tasks and minute allowances. A contractor evaluating the service should separate message collection from transferring a caller or writing into a scheduling system. This guide reviews public sources as of October 23, 2026; it is not an account test.

sections.title: Choose message intake or the additional assistant tasks.
paragraphs: The US pricing page describes Answer Pro as collecting caller details and a reason for calling, with portal messages and email or text delivery. Total Assistant Pro adds transfers, scheduling/calendar integration and CRM/custom forms. Its listed transfer charge is $0.25 per transferred call.

For your office, define what the receptionist may finish. Receiving an estimate request can end with a message for follow-up. Confirming a visit requires authority over the schedule and a usable appointment slot. Put those outcomes in separate acceptance tests rather than assuming that every captured request is a booking.
items: Message test: can the office identify the caller’s request and follow-up details?
Transfer test: what happens when the approved recipient does not answer?
Scheduling test: does the agreed workflow create the intended calendar record?

sections.title: Check the bill using rounded calls, not aggregate seconds.
paragraphs: Reception247’s terms measure receptionist minutes as time spent handling calls, including contacting staff during a transfer. They exclude after-call administration such as writing an emailed note. Incoming and outgoing calls are each rounded upward to a whole minute. The terms also state that displayed pricing assumes autopay enrollment.

Illustrative reconciliation only: suppose there are two separate calls, each lasting 40 seconds, with no additional handling time. Each rounds to one minute, producing two billable minutes from 80 seconds of conversation. Adding seconds first and rounding the combined duration would not follow the published per-call rule.

If both illustrative minutes fall within the plan allowance, they consume two included minutes. If the full allowance was already used before these calls, two Answer Pro 25-minute-plan overage minutes would cost 2 × $1.69 = $3.38. On a Total Assistant Pro plan, one transferred call would add the listed $0.25 transfer charge if applicable; any additional agent handling time must also be reconciled. These are declared examples, not actual usage or a complete invoice.
items: Compare individual call records with rounded billable minutes.
Identify which minutes remain included and which are excess.
Reconcile transferred-call count separately from handling duration.

sources.label: Reception247 rates and transfer charge; reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Verify the contractor workflow in the actual account.
paragraphs: The contractor page advertises appointment handling, tailored scripts, custom information collection and familiarity with ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro and Workiz. The pricing page names Calendly, HubSpot and Salesforce as examples in the higher plan family. These are published scope statements, not evidence that a particular customer account or workflow has been configured and tested.

Bring one representative request and the office’s actual rules to onboarding. Specify whether the receptionist should collect information, request a callback, propose a time or create a confirmed appointment. Check the destination record and notification against that instruction. A familiar software name does not identify which fields, permissions or actions are supported.

For a requested transfer, the FAQ describes voicemail as an option when staff are unavailable. Confirm the chosen fallback for your account and identify who reviews the resulting message. Do not tell callers that an attempted connection guarantees a conversation with the contractor.
items: Scheduling: verify work type, duration, service area and the permitted calendar action.
CRM/forms: verify required fields and where the submitted record appears.
Unavailable staff: verify the message destination and follow-up owner.

sections.title: Leave onboarding with a scope and billing decision.
paragraphs: The FAQ describes typical setup as the same day or within 24 hours, with complex needs handled separately. Treat that as the provider’s general description, not a guaranteed ready-to-route deadline for a custom scheduling or CRM arrangement.

The pricing page advertises monthly plan changes or cancellation without penalty or fees. Its linked Terms of Use separately refer to Terms and Conditions of Supply for service-specific provisions. Obtain the applicable enrollment and supply documents before relying on a complete billing or cancellation arrangement; the website terms are not necessarily the whole service agreement.

Finish with a written selection: plan family, included minutes, excess-minute rate, transfer charging, approved tasks and tested fallback. Review actual rounded usage after launch before changing allowances. A cheaper base subscription can describe a different task scope rather than the same service at a lower total cost.
items: Retain the applicable plan and billing documents with their review date.
Record any unresolved setup, calendar or CRM question explicitly.
Route customer calls only after the agreed outcomes are verified.

sources.label: Reception247 website and supply terms distinction; reviewed October 23, 2026

faqs.q: How do two separate 40-second calls affect the minute allowance?
faqs.a: Under the published per-call rounding rule, each uses one billable minute: two minutes total. That is an illustration with no additional handling time, not a customer invoice.

faqs.q: Does the contractor page prove my scheduling integration works?
faqs.a: No. It publishes supported service categories and software familiarity. Verify the agreed action, permissions and resulting record in your configured workflow before relying on it.

faqs.q: Are transfer time and the per-transfer charge the same thing?
faqs.a: No. The terms count agent handling time, including contacting staff during a transfer, as receptionist minutes. Total Assistant Pro pricing separately lists $0.25 per transferred call; confirm how the account applies both items.

takeaway: Match the plan to the task and verify the bill at the individual-call level.

title: Customer service call log: template and worked reconciliation
description: Use a blank call log template and a worked example to reconcile call events, repeat contacts, request ownership and the action still waiting for your office.
lead: Keep the telephone event and the service request as separate records.
intro: A useful call log preserves each call while showing which calls belong to the same request. Use the blank CSV and fictional worked example below to create an event ledger your office can reconcile. Four calls can represent two requests, one new inquiry and one existing-job question. This original template does not establish a Revo export, integration or booking feature.

overviewTable.caption: Worked example: fictional records from the downloadable event ledger
rows: Inbound reply about the same request
EX-A01 closed by EX-E03; CAL01 evidence
Inbound; question about existing job EX-J02

sections.title: Copy the blank ledger without inventing customer records
paragraphs: Download the header-only CSV. Keep one row per telephone event with event_id and request_id; timestamps and timezone; direction and authorized customer/job references; request_type; connection_result; request_outcome; and action snapshots: action_id, action_state, action_updated_at, closed_by_event_id, next_action, action_owner, due_at and evidence_reference. Use references instead of copying unnecessary personal details.

event_id identifies the particular call; request_id links related contacts about the same work. A repeated phone number alone is insufficient evidence of a shared request. When the relationship is uncertain, retain the call event with an unresolved request reference and send it for office review. Do not merge it merely to make the counts look tidy.

Record timestamps with an offset and the operating time zone. due_at belongs to the next action; it is not the call time. Leave job_reference empty if no job exists yet. The worked example uses the local time zone America/Tijuana and deliberately fictional EX-prefixed identifiers.
items: Keep stable event IDs from the source system where available; document any assigned substitute IDs.
connection_result records technical connection (connected or no_answer here); request_outcome records the business result (such as appointment_confirmed). Neither substitutes for action_state.
Use the authoritative scheduler or job record to confirm a result; a note saying booking requested is insufficient.

sources.label: Download blank call-log CSV; original Revo worksheet

sections.title: Reconcile four events into two requests
paragraphs: EX-E01 opens EX-A01 for EX-R01. EX-E02 records no_answer and a later open snapshot of EX-A01, not another lead. EX-E03 records connected and appointment_confirmed, supported by fictional calendar CAL01. Its EX-A01 snapshot is closed and names EX-E03 in closed_by_event_id. Earlier open snapshots remain unchanged as history. This scheduling closure does not establish completed field work.

EX-E04 belongs to EX-R02 and an existing job, EX-J02. The call was answered, but the customer’s job question still needs a coordinator. Answered therefore does not mean resolved. Keep that next action assigned to the Example coordinator, with its own due time.

The resulting reconciliation is four distinct call events, two service requests, one new-service inquiry, one confirmed appointment and one existing-job question awaiting follow-up. These are counts from the fictional file, not customer results, a conversion benchmark or a causal comparison of services.

Reconstruct the current action list by deduplicating identical event_id rows; flag conflicting versions for review. Group snapshots by action_id and select the greatest action_updated_at after parsing its offset. If equal timestamps disagree, stop for review rather than selecting arbitrarily. Keep only latest snapshots with action_state open. Never sum historical open snapshots. A later reopening requires an appended snapshot with a later timestamp and evidence; preserve the prior events.
items: Check event IDs first: importing the same EX-E02 twice must not create a fifth real call.
Check request links second: three contacts about EX-R01 remain three events attached to one request.
Latest EX-A01 snapshot: EX-E03, closed, no due action. Latest EX-A02 snapshot: EX-E04, open, Example coordinator due 10:00. Exactly one action remains open.

sections.title: Check the source view before copying a report
paragraphs: Housecall Pro’s July 16, 2026 Call Log Guide distinguishes missed, answered inbound, outbound and voicemail views. It says its emailed CSV export follows the current view and applied filters and is limited to 5,000 calls. Those documented product rules were reviewed October 23, 2026. They do not describe every provider’s export or a Revo capability.

A filtered export can be correct and still omit the events needed for reconciliation. Record the selected view, date range, time zone, filters and export time beside the saved file. Compare a small known set with the source log. If the system creates separate transfer legs, ask what each identifier represents before deciding whether two rows are duplicate events.

Import original source data into a preserved copy before mapping it into this template. Keep a stable import reference. Correct a mistaken request link with a dated explanation rather than erasing the original telephone event. This preserves the difference between a data correction and a call that did not occur.

sources.label: Housecall Pro Call Log Guide; reviewed October 23, 2026

sections.title: Close the office action with evidence, not a cleared badge
paragraphs: Reconstruct the latest snapshot per action_id before reviewing due actions. Preserve every historical event. For a closed action, closed_by_event_id identifies its closing event and evidence_reference identifies the supporting record. Earlier owners and due times remain history, not current assignments.

A read or played message is not, on its own, a completed customer response. Housecall Pro’s guide says viewing missed-call details or playing a voicemail affects its badge count. That is a useful example of why an interface notification and the underlying office task need separate checks.

Use the blank CSV as an operating template, not a replacement for the authoritative customer, job or calendar system. Before storing real records, apply your business’s existing access and retention arrangements. Reconcile the next-action list with those source systems at the review interval your office actually uses.
items: Pending inquiry: identify the person responsible and the next permitted action.
Completed scheduling action: link to the actual confirmation record.
Existing-job question: preserve the job reference and the unresolved request even after the call ends.

sources.label: Housecall Pro badge behavior; reviewed October 23, 2026

faqs.q: Why keep both an event ID and a request ID?
faqs.a: An event ID distinguishes each call. A request ID links related contacts about the same work. In the example, three different events link to EX-R01 without becoming three new inquiries.

faqs.q: What is the outstanding action after the four example calls?
faqs.a: The latest EX-A01 snapshot is EX-E03 (closed); the latest EX-A02 snapshot is EX-E04 (open). Only EX-A02 remains due, assigned to the Example coordinator. Earlier open EX-A01 snapshots remain history. Field work completion is not established.

faqs.q: Does the template import directly into Revo or Housecall Pro?
faqs.a: No integration is asserted. This is a neutral CSV ledger. Map only fields supported by your authorized source system and preserve the original export.

takeaway: Preserve every real call event, link it to the right request and close only the action supported by an office record.

title: Best answering services for pest control: compare the work
description: Compare pest-control answering services by recurring accounts, treatment booking, pest-software access and the exceptions your office must handle.
lead: Choose for an initial treatment, an existing plan and the record each call leaves.
intro: For a pest-control company, the best answering service depends on whether it must sell an approved plan, change an existing treatment or only capture a request. This shortlist compares Slingshot, Sameday and Rosie using their own documentation checked October 23, 2026. Published by Revo; no controlled performance tests or universal ranking are claimed.

sections.title: Slingshot: pest-trained service across new and existing accounts
paragraphs: Slingshot describes pest-trained agents supported by AI, with sales, scheduling, payment collection and customer support. It names Voice for Pest, PestRoutes, PestPac, ServSuite and Briostack. Its FAQ includes existing-customer calls and outbound payment or rescheduling work; communications and recordings are visible in Central Inbox. Pricing is customized per minute; its stated average onboarding is two to three weeks.

Shortlist this documented model when your office wants a person to handle account work as well as new inquiries. Before buying, separate permission to collect a payment from permission to change a plan or waive a fee. Ask it to demonstrate your actual software, account permissions and audit trail; the named list does not prove every action in every account.
items: Quote scope: new sales versus existing-account support, outbound work and minute treatment.
Demonstration: an existing customer requests a repeat visit under a plan; show the account record and the approval boundary.

sources.label: Slingshot pest-control service and detailed FAQ

sections.title: Sameday: AI treatment and recurring-service workflows
paragraphs: Sameday’s pest-control page describes AI intake by pest and property type, treatment scheduling and recurring-plan offers. It also describes changing an existing recurring appointment and writing the change back to the CRM. These are vendor-described workflows, not observations from our test calls.

Shortlist it when the desired output is a treatment or recurring-service update in supported software. Ask which operations are enabled for your pest platform and plan. Have it distinguish a first treatment, an inspection and an existing-plan visit: those can require different durations, eligibility and approval. Do not accept a generic calendar event as proof that the correct recurring service was updated.
items: Verify allowed plan language, service types, area and route availability.
Request the before-and-after account record for a reschedule, including a failed-write fallback.

sections.title: Rosie: separate message taking from higher-tier scheduling
paragraphs: Rosie has a dedicated pest-control offer. Its pricing distinguishes Professional’s texted appointment link from Scale’s direct calendar booking and warm/live transfers; Growth adds waterfall transfers. The page also lists call summaries, transcripts, recordings and email/text notifications across plans.

Shortlist this when a documented message or supported calendar workflow meets the requirement. title: Virtual reception services for lead qualification: compare
description: Compare receptionist services by qualification rules, rejected and uncertain inquiries, delivered records and the evidence your office needs to act.
lead: Buy a decision trail and usable handoff, not a qualified-lead label.
intro: This comparison examines Smith.ai, AnswerConnect and Ruby by how documented screening becomes an office handoff. It covers rule design, delivery and uncertain answers, rather than repeating an intake question list. Published by Revo; official sources checked October 23, 2026. No qualified-lead yield or conversion improvement was measured.

sections.title: Smith.ai: explicit screening decisions and a separate intake stage
paragraphs: Smith.ai’s current screening page describes custom criteria, AI-first intake and human escalation for complex situations, with dashboard notes, summaries and call metadata. Its dated March 26, 2025 product announcement describes up to three yes/no qualification questions in addition to location/service screening, with a disqualifying answer ending the call. Confirm current package limits; the older announcement is evidence of that documented design, not a universal limit on all intake today.

This is a useful candidate when the business wants explicit decision gates. Ask it to show the actual rule order and the record for a rejected caller, not only a successful intake. A vague answer such as “I think the property is in your area” must have a reviewed handling rule; do not silently convert uncertainty into a negative answer. Confirm the human handoff scope and terms for your chosen AI or staffed package.
items: Request: applied rule version, answer captured, screening decision and exception reason.
Keep qualification gates separate from the longer intake questions asked after a caller passes.

sections.title: AnswerConnect: live scripted scoring against your criteria
paragraphs: AnswerConnect’s inbound-sales service describes a team using a scripting tool to score leads against client criteria and customize scripts during setup. Its small-business explanation says receptionists screen using your criteria and send the details afterward. Those descriptions establish a staffed screening model, not a particular home-service scoring formula or a guaranteed qualified lead.

Shortlist it if a person working from your scoring policy is important. Supply the score inputs, mandatory disqualifiers and the treatment of missing answers. Ask for the exact delivered fields and destination, including the record for an inquiry that fails the score. The reviewed pages do not specify a portable rule-version audit field or your CRM mapping; treat those as demonstration requirements.
items: Separate mandatory service-area exclusion from a preference such as requested timing.
Require an unscored or needs-review path when a required answer is unavailable.

sections.title: Ruby: configurable information collection with live reception
paragraphs: Ruby documents live receptionists, call handling instructions that can be updated, lead capture and notifications through email, text or its app. Its plan page says the information collected can be customized. These sources do not establish a specific numerical scoring engine or the same automatic rejection behavior as the Smith.ai announcement.

Shortlist Ruby when live collection and an accountable office decision are more important than a published scoring mechanism. Ask what the receptionist may decide and what remains a message for your team. Demonstrate a caller who changes an answer, an existing customer misidentified as a new prospect and a request needing a specialist; confirm the resulting notification contains the uncertainty rather than an unsupported qualified label.
items: Confirm the actual questions and call handling update process.
Request a sample delivered message and prove that the responsible person can retrieve it.

sections.title: Compare the same evidence packet from every finalist
paragraphs: Use this original fictional acceptance case: the business serves residential properties in its approved ZIP list and offers plumbing repairs but not restoration work. The caller reports water damage, cannot yet confirm the service address and asks for a repair visit. The correct business decision is not supplied by a vendor’s qualified label: preserve the missing address, the requested work and the boundary between plumbing and restoration for office review.

Ask each finalist for one example that passes all mandatory rules, one clearly outside the service area and the uncertain example above. Compare the original answers, applied rule version, decision with reason, unresolved field, delivery destination and named follow-up owner. A CRM contact created without those details is a different deliverable from a reviewable screening record.

Repeat the uncertain case after a documented rule change and check that the new version governs it. This is a proposed evaluation protocol, not a claim that any listed provider already exports every field. Confirm what is included, requires configuration or is unavailable before selecting a plan.
items: Do not count existing-customer service calls as new qualified prospects.
Ask how rejected and uncertain inquiries remain available for review.
A screening decision does not promise a booking, completed job or revenue.

faqs.a: Define that with your business before setup. Preserve an unknown value and a needs-review path rather than assuming missing means no.

faqs.a: No. The comparison distinguishes explicit gates, live scripted scoring and configurable live collection. Verify the exact mechanism and output in the proposed package.

sections.title: ServiceTitan Voice Agent: permission and job-type controls
paragraphs: ServiceTitan’s Basic Phones/Phones Pro setup guide, updated October 22, marks the feature Early Access for specific accounts. Booking, rescheduling and cancellation require both the overall capability and the applicable job-type toggle. This is a concrete control to check when plumbing repairs may be booked but installation estimates follow a different policy.

Its FAQ describes unbooked-call follow-up tags and email summaries. The same FAQ still lists a launch limitation on adding notes, summaries or transcripts to booked job records. Ask the provider to reconcile that limitation for your account rather than assuming a call summary is attached to every booked job. sections.title: Avoca: compare the job record and CSR handoff
paragraphs: Avoca’s ServiceTitan page describes sending customer details, appointment times, service information, booking source and conversation notes to ServiceTitan. Its inbound page describes contextual escalation to a CSR. Neither description establishes that every account has the same permissions to change or cancel an existing appointment.

For an HVAC/plumbing evaluation, request the exact record produced for a repair, maintenance visit and estimate. Then ask for an appointment-change case and an integration write failure. Require the proposed scope to identify whether the service changes the record, captures a request or escalates it. A transcript saying “booked” is insufficient if the job did not arrive in the authoritative system.
items: Check the service type, address and appointment on the actual returned job record.
Identify the receiving CSR and the fallback when that person is unavailable.

sections.title: Sameday: distinguish trade workflow from confirmed field availability
paragraphs: Sameday’s plumbing page describes applying a business’s urgency rules and routing calls to an on-call plumber. Its HVAC page describes service versus maintenance and install workflows. The ServiceTitan integration page documents customer-data synchronization, scheduling/service information and on-call notification.

Treat those as documented workflow claims to validate with your configured service area, job types and calendar. A water-damage caller may need plumbing intake, restoration or an escalation outside your offered work. Have the business specify that boundary. Do not require the agent to diagnose the cause or treat an urgent label as proof that a qualified technician has accepted the job.
items: Request the exact trade/job-type mapping and the booking response.
Show what the caller hears when the requested time is unavailable.

sections.title: Rosie: a calendar workflow is a separate buying option
paragraphs: Rosie’s Professional plan sends an appointment link; Scale lists direct calendar booking and warm/live transfers. Growth adds multiple transfer destinations. Those published tier boundaries matter if the office expects an urgent request to reach a person rather than receive a booking link.

The reviewed pricing evidence does not establish a native ServiceTitan job write or the permission structure above. A supported calendar may be sufficient for estimate requests while the dispatcher creates the final job. If your office needs a service-board record during the call, do not mark a calendar event as equivalent without demonstrating the intervening workflow.
items: Compare the selected plan and supported calendar, not only the term appointment booking.
Verify transfer behavior against an unavailable recipient and the selected tier.

paragraphs: These are original proposed acceptance cases, not measured provider results. First, request routine maintenance where availability exists: inspect the stored service type and appointment. Second, change an existing plumbing appointment: verify that the original record changes rather than a duplicate job being created.

Third, report water entering a room but request work outside the contractor’s scope. Check that the caller’s words and unsupported-work boundary reach the authorized office contact without an invented diagnosis or arrival promise. Fourth, request a fully booked same-day window while the escalation recipient is unavailable. Record the unbooked request, attempted contact, fallback and next owner.

For each finalist, mark an operation documented, demonstrated on the proposed setup or unverified. Confirm who may accept a job and which hours the field team actually serves. These answering products are not interchangeable with a dispatch commitment; no capabilities of the listed providers are attributed to Revo.

Ask where unbooked requests are reviewed and who owns them.

title: Plan 24/7 phone coverage: shifts, peaks and backup owners
description: Build a weekly phone-coverage plan with time windows, peak triggers, absence backups and accountable follow-up, using a blank CSV and fictional week.
lead: Account for every interval and test the person or service expected to answer.
intro: Planning 24/7 phone coverage requires an assignment for every time window, a response to peaks and an owner when someone is absent. Use the downloadable templates to turn those decisions into a weekly plan. The example is fictional and all its rows are planned, not verified. It is not a recommended headcount or proof of any provider’s uptime.

sections.title: Measure demand by interval before assigning the week
paragraphs: Collect your own call arrivals and handling time by interval, including simultaneous demand, unanswered calls and work performed after the conversation. Separate new requests from existing-customer work. A monthly total cannot show whether a quiet night and a short morning burst need different handling.

Amazon Connect’s documentation distinguishes forecasting contact volume and handle time, capacity planning and individual scheduling. Its time-zone documentation also distinguishes forecast/download time zones. Those product concepts inform the planning questions here; neither Amazon scheduling nor workforce automation is asserted as a Revo feature.

Use one explicit operating time zone and dates in your worksheet. Choose interval lengths that expose your observed peaks. The example uses four six-hour blocks only to illustrate the assignment ledger; split those blocks where your records show a peak, break, training session or change of owner. The grid is not a staffing calculation.
items: Record the source period, interval, time zone and omitted call types alongside the demand data.
Confirm team availability rather than deriving staffing solely from answered-call averages.

sources.label: Amazon Connect forecasting, capacity and scheduling concepts
Amazon Connect forecast and download time zones

sections.title: Fill the coverage ledger and keep verification separate
paragraphs: The blank CSV contains headers only. The fictional example contains 28 rows for October 26–November 1, 2026 in America/Phoenix, using start-inclusive/end-exclusive hours from 0 to 24. It assigns example roles, never real employees or contact information. Four rows cover each calendar day; the hours add to 168 for that seven-day example, which does not claim the same total for every time zone or daylight-saving week.

Each row identifies the primary answerer, a backup, the unavailable-primary rule, an office-defined peak trigger and peak owner, an authorized urgent-escalation role, the routine-review time and owner, and verification evidence/status. The next routine-review time concerns office follow-up; it is not the time that calls begin to be answered. In this fictional policy, office reviews occur Monday–Friday at 08:00, 12:00 and 18:00. routine_review_at is the first such review at or after the end of the entire row interval, not the review following only its first call. Thus weekday 00–06 goes to 08:00 that same day; 06–12 goes to 12:00; 12–18 goes to 18:00; and overnight/weekend work waits until the next applicable review. Adjust that stated policy to your actual team before use.

Check that each day starts at 0, ends at 24 and has no overlap or gap. Then confirm the named roles correspond to contracted or scheduled coverage. Keep status planned_not_verified until an authorized test and evidence support a verified state. A filled cell alone does not prove someone will answer.
items: Replace every EX-role with a confirmed responsibility before operational use.
Do not fill an unknown backup with the primary person under a different label.
Keep field-service escalation separate from the service or person answering the phone.
Require routine_review_at to be at least the interval end for every row; then confirm it is the first available review under the declared policy.

sections.title: Resolve a peak and an absence in the same interval
paragraphs: Worked planning example: Tuesday’s 12–18 block names the office as primary. A team training session from 13–14 means that label is insufficient. Split it into 12–13, 13–14 and 14–18. For 13–14, name the confirmed backup as primary, its separate fallback, the same business instruction version and the office person who will review resulting requests. Keep the original plan as a dated prior version.

Now suppose observed arrivals show a burst during 14–15. Split that interval again if needed. Define the trigger from the system you actually use, such as an agreed queue condition or unavailable primary, and identify who activates extra coverage and who returns the normal route. Do not assume software removes concurrent-call limits or that an on-call technician can simultaneously answer every overflow call.

If no backup is confirmed, mark that interval unresolved and do not describe the plan as reliable 24/7 coverage. Change the assignment or the public expectation before relying on it. This example concerns responsibility and switching, not employment-law advice or a prescribed shift pattern.

The revised-example CSV implements those Tuesday splits: 12–13, 13–14, 14–15 and 15–18 replace the original 12–18 row. It has 31 rows, still covering 168 hours without overlaps. The training interval names a replacement primary and a different secondary backup. All rows remain planned_not_verified; role acceptance and tests are still required. Each split row uses the first scheduled office review at or after its own end; the training and peak rows therefore point to Tuesday 18:00 in this example.
items: Primary absent: replace the interval assignment, confirm fallback and record acceptance.
Peak active: record the trigger, activation owner, capacity evidence and return-to-normal step.
Routine backlog: confirm a review owner and time even when the answering layer remains available.

sections.title: Accept coverage at handoffs, not only during normal hours
paragraphs: Use consenting test callers in an approved window; this article reports no calls actually placed. Test just before and after a handoff, an unavailable primary, an unavailable escalation contact, and an office-defined peak condition through a provider-supported method. Record expected answerer, actual endpoint, business instruction version, result and evidence reference.

Have the next owner acknowledge the handoff and inspect the first pending request. Where a provider answers continuously, test the change in business instructions and recipients as well as the connection. Phone answering, acceptance by an on-call employee and the next routine office review are three different responsibilities.

Review the plan when demand or availability changes. Keep a version, effective date, decision owner and restoration instructions so a temporary absence route does not become permanent by accident. The worksheet is neutral; it does not implement routing, schedule employees or establish a Revo integration.
items: Treat planned, tested and unresolved intervals as different statuses.
Check business and provider schedules against holidays and the selected time zone.
Do not claim a coverage test measures long-term uptime or search-engine indexing.

title: 24/7 Live Receptionist Services: Human Coverage Compared
description: Compare PATLive, ReceptionHQ, Ruby and AnswerConnect by overnight human coverage, staffing location, language hours, holiday limits and tasks.
lead: If you need a person to answer at midnight, start with the human coverage schedule. A service can keep its phone system running all night while switching callers to automation, voicemail or a different reception team. The buying question is who conducts the conversation at the hour your customers call, in the language they need, with permission to complete the required task.

sections.title: Human coverage comparison
paragraphs:

[Receptionist FAQ](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq/receptionist-services) |

Davinci's wording uses “EST.” Ask whether its operational schedule follows Eastern daylight time during the relevant months or a fixed standard-time offset. Record the answer against an actual date. Its after-hours system can route calls or offer voicemail, but that does not establish a human receptionist conversation at that hour. It belongs outside an all-hours-human shortlist unless a separately documented offering meets your requirement.

sections.title: Language coverage and off-hours costs
paragraphs:
Treat language availability as its own schedule. A bilingual option on an account does not necessarily cover every overnight call.

| Service | Documented language scope | Surcharge or unresolved commercial term |
|---|---|---|
| PATLive | English 24/7; Spanish 8am–10pm ET, 365 days a year | Spanish included without an additional language fee; request any night/holiday billing terms in writing. [Bilingual service](https://www.patlive.com/solutions/bilingual-receptionists/) |

Obtain amount and applicable dates. [FAQ](https://www.receptionhq.com/service/live-call-answering/virtual-receptionist-appointment-scheduling/) |
| Ruby | English and Spanish advertised around the clock | Ask for language, holiday and task-specific charges in the selected plan. [Bilingual coverage](https://www.ruby.com/solutions/live-virtual-receptionists/) |
| AnswerConnect | Language-specific hours not established by the reviewed answering page | Page includes 24/7 service in every plan; obtain itemized terms for your requested workflow. [Plan scope](https://www.answerconnect.com/services/answering-services) |
| Davinci | Language-specific hours unresolved in the reviewed FAQ | First establish whether any proposed service meets your required human hours. [FAQ](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq/receptionist-services) |

For ReceptionHQ, confirm how “MST” maps to your location on both summer and winter dates. Do not convert that label to another zone from memory. The quote should specify the timezone or offset used to determine charges.

A US business can be served by a human team in another country. Decide separately whether your requirement concerns the person's location, the language of the conversation, the hours covered or data-access terms. Eliminating candidates on an unstated assumption makes the comparison less useful.

sections.title: Three acceptance cards to complete before forwarding customer calls
paragraphs:
These are proposed buyer tests, not completed provider evaluations. Agree on an authorized test with each shortlisted service. Use a fictional customer and a task permitted by the proposed package. Leave observed results blank until the test takes place.

| Card | Night call | Holiday call | No-answer handoff |
|---|---|---|---|
| Declared date, local time and timezone | ___ | ___; holiday name: ___ | ___ |
| Person/service expected to answer | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Required language | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Task allowed in the written scope | ___ | ___ | Attempt transfer, then agreed fallback: ___ |
| Staffing-location requirement, if any | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Quoted surcharge and billing unit | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Written evidence / agreement reference | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Observed result | ___ | ___ | ___ |
| Unresolved issue and owner | ___ | ___ | ___ |

**Night call:** Choose an hour outside your office schedule, not just five minutes after closing. Ask the receptionist to perform the exact permitted action, such as capturing an inquiry or making an authorized booking. A friendly conversation alone does not demonstrate task completion.

**Holiday call:** Use a specific holiday that matters to your business. If testing on that date is not practical before purchase, retain the contractual answer as untested evidence and schedule a later authorized check. Do not mark a weekday demonstration as a holiday pass.

**No-answer handoff:** Arrange for the intended recipient not to answer. Check what the caller hears next and where the unresolved request goes. Do not confuse an attempted transfer with someone accepting responsibility for the work.

A failed card should identify the missing requirement: person, time, language, task, fallback or cost. That lets you ask for a narrower fix instead of accepting a vague assurance that the service is available all day.

sections.title: Choose the service that meets the required call, not the longest feature list
paragraphs:
Make overnight human conversation a pass/fail requirement if that is what your customers need. Then filter by language hours, permitted tasks and location constraints. Compare commercial terms only among the candidates still eligible.

For billing detail, use the separate [PATLive pricing review](/ai-answering-service/patlive-pricing) and [ReceptionHQ pricing review](/ai-answering-service/receptionhq-pricing). Keep this decision focused on who will answer and what that person can do.

Revo is an AI answering service, not a staffed human reception provider. If you are still deciding whether every call needs a person, [compare AI answering with a live receptionist](/ai-answering-service/compare/ai-vs-live-receptionist). If AI handling could fit part of your coverage, [review Revo’s service](https://www.revoapp.ai/) and ask which plan and configuration support your required next step.

takeaway: Choose the service that meets the required call, not the longest feature list
