lead: Breezy’s AI receptionist sits inside a broader front-office package. Before comparing its subscription with an answering-only service, decide where you want customer records to live and who should configure the connection.
intro: Breezy’s AI receptionist sits inside a broader front-office package. Before comparing its subscription with an answering-only service, decide where you want customer records to live and who should configure the connection.

sections.title: Start with the package path
paragraphs:
Breezy’s published package grid distinguishes self-serve Professional and Growth plans from done-for-you Accelerate and White Glove arrangements. Its Smart CRM page describes connecting an existing CRM as part of done-for-you onboarding. That deserves more attention than a generic “integrates with your CRM” label. [Breezy Smart CRM](https://getbreezy.app/home/features/smart-crm)

Use this original purchase map to frame the sales conversation:

```text
Where should the office manage the customer record?
    |
    +-- Breezy's bundled CRM
    |      -> Compare self-serve packages
    |      -> Check users and required channels
    |      -> Name the person responsible for setup and changes
    |
    +-- Existing CRM remains authoritative
           -> Ask for the managed onboarding scope
           -> Name the exact CRM and required operations
           -> Obtain ownership, support and change terms

Either path -> demonstrate the actual contact and appointment records
            -> resolve usage and commercial terms -> decide
```

This map does not establish that every requested connection is available. It identifies the evidence needed to choose the package rather than discovering the implementation gap afterward.

sections.title: Published plan differences
paragraphs:
The following monthly amounts and limits appear in the pricing grid on Breezy’s scheduling page. They are subscription entries, not an all-in quote or a per-minute rate. The dedicated pricing URL could not be directly retrieved during this review; verify the selected billing option before ordering.

| Package | Displayed monthly amount | Users | Published channel scope | Setup category |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Professional | $50 | 1 | Phone and SMS | Self-serve |
| Growth | $150 | Up to 3 | Phone, SMS and web chat | Self-serve |
| Accelerate | $750 | Up to 10 | Phone, SMS, email, WhatsApp and social | Done for you |
| White Glove | Custom | Unlimited | All channels as described by the provider | Done for you / custom |

The grid lists CRM and scheduling on Professional and Growth, with broader CRM integration and managed scope on the higher arrangements. It does not establish a voice-minute allowance or additional-usage price in the material reviewed here. Ask what is measured, what is included and what happens when usage exceeds any applicable limit. [Breezy scheduling and plan grid](https://getbreezy.app/home/features/ai-scheduling)

Do not divide a subscription amount by an assumed call count to invent a rate. Likewise, “custom” does not imply a particular minimum, and a channel named in the grid does not prove every operation works through that channel.

sections.title: Built-in CRM and an existing CRM are different commitments
paragraphs:
If you plan to use the bundled CRM, ask which records the office will maintain there and how staff will access them. Decide whether the tool becomes the primary customer record or a lead workspace that hands work to another system.

If your existing CRM remains authoritative, have the proposal name it. Ask which actions the connection performs: create a contact, update an existing contact, attach conversation details, create an appointment or send a request for staff action. These are purchasing requirements to resolve, not verified Breezy connector capabilities.

A vendor can offer a managed setup without taking over every future administrative task. Identify who maintains business hours, staff access, routing instructions and changes to the destination system. Obtain those responsibilities in writing before relying on the phrase “done for you.”

sections.title: Distinguish the scheduling actor
paragraphs:
Breezy’s receptionist page advertises AI answering and appointment booking. Its scheduling page separately describes client self-service for changes and cancellations. A customer changing an appointment in a self-service interface is different from an AI completing the same operation during a phone call. [Breezy AI receptionist](https://getbreezy.app/home/features/voicemail-receptionist) and [scheduling service](https://getbreezy.app/home/features/ai-scheduling)

For any required operation, record who does it. Leave phone-based rescheduling or cancellation unresolved unless the seller demonstrates that exact action for the proposed setup. Do not turn a general scheduling description into proof of every lifecycle operation.

sections.title: Trace one customer through the proposed package
paragraphs:
Use this original demonstration record with fictional data and the provider’s permission. It is not a completed Breezy test. The example focuses on the package and destination being purchased; technical failure testing belongs in a separate integration review.

Test customer: `DEMO-BREEZY-01`. Request: an estimate appointment for an approved service at a location your business covers.

| Evidence | Bundled-CRM path | Existing-CRM path |
|---|---|---|
| Proposed package and billing option | ___ | ___ |
| Person or AI taking the request | ___ | ___ |
| Contact record created or matched | Breezy record ID: ___ | Authoritative CRM ID: ___; other copy, if any: ___ |
| Appointment result | Appointment ID/status: ___ | Destination record ID/status: ___ |
| Office workspace used afterward | ___ | ___ |
| Actor for a later appointment change | ___ | ___ |
| Setup and ongoing-change owner | ___ | ___ |
| Observed result and unresolved question | ___ | ___ |

Ask the demonstrator to show the records rather than relying only on the conversation. If the outcome is a request for staff review, describe it that way. If two systems contain copies, identify which one the office should trust and who resolves a disagreement.

Do not use real customer information merely to make the sales demonstration realistic. A fictional contact is enough to establish which screens, records and staff responsibilities are involved.

sections.title: Resolve the remaining purchase terms
paragraphs:
Ask for a written answer to five questions:

1. What voice, messaging or other usage is included, and how are additional charges calculated?
2. Which exact CRM operations and channels are included in this package?
3. Who completes setup and maintains the configuration afterward?
4. What happens to the business number, contact records and appointment data if the service ends?
5. Which required scheduling actions remain with the office or the customer’s self-service interface?

An unanswered term should remain open. Do not assume that data export, number ownership or a particular integration is included simply because the product is presented as a complete front office.

sections.title: Choose the scope your office will use
paragraphs:
Breezy may belong on the shortlist when you want to evaluate its bundled front-office tools or its documented managed CRM setup. If your requirement is narrower, compare the complete package against an answering-focused alternative instead of treating every included tool as necessary value.

For Revo, [review the current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) and ask the team to confirm the software and workflow you need. This guide establishes no native Revo connection to Breezy or any CRM mentioned here, and it makes no claim that either service performs better or costs less for equivalent work.

takeaway: Choose the scope your office will use

title: SkipCalls AI receptionist pricing: fair use and plan questions
description: Review SkipCalls’ published monthly and annual prices, call-based fair-use limits and unresolved plan wording before choosing the service.
lead: SkipCalls markets AI answering with unlimited minutes, but its linked fair-use policy discusses call allowances and named plans. A useful price comparison must account for both—not turn a short headline into an unlimited-use guarantee.
intro: SkipCalls markets AI answering with unlimited minutes, but its linked fair-use policy discusses call allowances and named plans. A useful price comparison must account for both—not turn a short headline into an unlimited-use guarantee.

sections.title: Read the offer on the current page
paragraphs:
The pricing page opened for this review showed **$29.99 monthly** or **$249.99 annually**, with the annual amount also displayed as $20.83 per month billed yearly. It advertised a seven-day trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. The cancellation FAQ said service continues through the paid period. These are the provider’s published statements; confirm the terms for the exact purchase channel before paying. [SkipCalls pricing](https://skipcalls.com/pricing)

Do not mistake the annual monthly equivalent for a monthly payment option. Record the amount due, billing period, renewal arrangement and required cancellation action in the offer you actually select. A trial or guarantee also needs its applicable start date and process confirmed.

Search results or older references may show different numbers. Use the current written offer for your decision rather than combining an older price with newer features.

sections.title: Compare calls with minutes
paragraphs:
SkipCalls’ fair-use page states 200 calls per month for Starter and 350 for PRO. It says call length does not change the call count, excludes unwanted spam from fair usage, and describes seasonal peaks as acceptable. For consistently higher usage, it describes contacting the customer about a more suitable plan rather than automatic cutoff or surprise charges. These are policy statements, not an independently verified billing result. [SkipCalls fair-use policy](https://skipcalls.com/fair-usage)

That gives an office a different planning unit from minutes. Count ordinary new inquiries, existing-customer calls and follow-ups separately when describing your workload to the seller. Do not convert a call allowance into a guaranteed number of minutes by multiplying it by a guessed average duration.

Ask what “consistently” means for your account and what written terms would apply if your volume grows. A policy allowing a seasonal peak is not evidence that sustained volume of any size is included at the same price.

sections.title: Resolve the plan wording before comparing the total
paragraphs:
The public material reviewed was not fully aligned. The pricing FAQ described no tiers or upsells, while its comparison table marked CRM integration as available on PRO. The linked fair-use page separately named Starter, PRO, Business and Enterprise arrangements. [SkipCalls pricing](https://skipcalls.com/pricing) [SkipCalls fair-use policy](https://skipcalls.com/fair-usage)

This review does not decide which wording controls a specific subscription. Ask SkipCalls to identify, in writing:

- The exact plan attached to the monthly or annual offer.
- Its call allowance and treatment of sustained higher volume.
- Whether the needed CRM or calendar operation is included.
- Any conditions that differ between the app and web purchase paths.
- The applicable renewal, cancellation and refund terms.

Keep unresolved items marked as unresolved. Do not assume either that every advertised feature is included or that an additional charge necessarily applies.

The linked terms destination did not provide readable terms text in this review. That limits verification of contractual details; the marketing FAQ should not be presented as a complete account agreement.

sections.title: Inspect what the integration creates
paragraphs:
SkipCalls’ integration page describes different outcomes for different systems. Its Housecall Pro entry claims in-call job booking with customer and service-address matching. Its Jobber entry describes creating clients and work requests, with transcripts and recording links. Those are vendor-described workflows, not interchangeable booking guarantees or tests performed here. [SkipCalls integrations](https://skipcalls.com/integrations)

A contractor evaluating the service should name the required result. Is a work request awaiting office review enough, or must the system create an authorized calendar booking? Ask for a demonstration of the specific operation in the proposed account and plan.

The same page lists calendar tools, CRM connections, notifications and automation options. A listed logo does not settle permissions, configuration, supported fields or exception behavior. Review your required operation rather than the total number of integrations.

sections.title: Use a small set of decisive acceptance checks
paragraphs:
These are proposed checks using authorized non-live demonstrations and fictional details. No test calls or customer records were created for this guide.

1. **New inquiry:** Verify the callback number, service address and requested work in the resulting record.
2. **Existing customer:** Confirm the request belongs to the correct customer and property.
3. **Booking requirement:** Inspect the destination record; distinguish a request from a confirmed appointment.
4. **Unavailable connection:** Establish what the caller hears and who receives the unfinished task.
5. **Usage review:** Ask how the account exposes counted calls and how unwanted calls are handled under its policy.
6. **Plan confirmation:** Match the demonstrated features to the written offer rather than a generic sales example.

Do not treat a pleasant demo voice as proof that the office can use the resulting work.

sections.title: Compare with Revo on the same scope
paragraphs:
Use the current written offer from each provider, including call handling, records, required connections and remaining staff work. SkipCalls’ public fair-use language is call-based; do not compare it directly with another provider’s minute allowance as though they were the same unit.

Review [Revo’s current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) and confirm the specific workflow directly. This page does not establish a Revo connection to Housecall Pro, Jobber or SkipCalls, or claim either provider is cheaper for your workload.

**Are unlimited minutes the same as unlimited calls?** Not in the fair-use policy reviewed here, which uses named call allowances.

**Which SkipCalls plan includes the required CRM connection?** Public wording reviewed was inconsistent. Obtain confirmation for the exact offer before relying on it.

**Does the published booking claim establish a completed field-service job record?** Only the supported workflow and its actual resulting record can settle that. Ask for the operation your office needs.

sections.title: Published packages and the purchase boundary
paragraphs:
| Arrangement | Published price basis | Concurrency | Telephony / support boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free test environment | $5 in test credits, approximately 30 minutes | 1 call | One inbound number; self-serve and AI support |
| Starter | $0.16 per minute; up to 30,000 minutes monthly | 5 calls | Number provisioning listed separately; self-serve and AI support |
| Enterprise | Custom annual arrangement | Contracted capacity | Bring-your-own SIP, managed setup and human support listed |

The Free card also displays $0 per minute; read that alongside its limited credits rather than as unlimited free calling. Starter’s 30,000-minute figure is a published plan limit, not 30,000 free minutes. The comparison table lists Starter number provisioning at $2 per number; confirm its billing interval. [Callers.ai pricing](https://www.callers.ai/pricing/)

A plan’s concurrent-call limit is different from its monthly usage. Buying another number does not establish more account capacity. Use your own required overlap and have the provider explain the applicable limit for the proposed configuration.

sections.title: Resolve the telephony and support differences
paragraphs:
Callers’ voice page describes connections through Twilio, SIP or Telnyx and retaining existing numbers. It also says a dedicated customer success manager guides setup on every plan. The pricing table is narrower: bring-your-own SIP and a dedicated manager are Enterprise features. Do not silently apply the broader product-page wording to Starter. [Callers voice product](https://www.callers.ai/channels/voice/) and [plan comparison](https://www.callers.ai/pricing/)

Ask which statement governs the package offered to your company. A useful answer names the plan, supported phone arrangement, setup owner and included support, rather than repeating that the platform connects to business systems.

The pricing page also contains a waitlist banner alongside purchase and trial prompts. Confirm whether the selected arrangement is available to your account and when access can begin. A visible price is not proof that your business can activate the required configuration immediately. [Callers.ai pricing](https://www.callers.ai/pricing/)

sections.title: Map your current phone arrangement to the proposed plan
paragraphs:
This is an original purchasing worksheet. It does not establish compatibility with your carrier or authorize a number change.

| Your requirement | Evidence needed from the seller | Plan accepted in writing | Remaining owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Use a newly supplied inbound number | Number availability, provisioning charges and account ownership | ___ | ___ |
| Keep the public business number through a supported route | Exact carrier-to-service arrangement; who configures and tests it | ___ | ___ |
| Bring existing telephony through SIP | Confirmation that the selected package supports that setup | ___ | ___ |
| Handle the office’s required overlapping calls | Account limit, treatment of transfers and the next caller above the limit | ___ | ___ |
| Receive human setup help | Named included service, contact route and responsibilities | ___ | ___ |

Keeping your advertised number and bringing your own telephony are not interchangeable requirements. A forwarded call can reach a new number without establishing that the agent platform accepts your existing SIP arrangement. Ask the provider to draw the actual path; leave any unverified step unresolved.

For the underlying operational distinctions, use the separate [number porting and forwarding guide](/ai-answering-service/phone-number-porting) and [simultaneous-call-capacity guide](/ai-answering-service/simultaneous-call-capacity). This page’s job is to connect those requirements to Callers’ documented package boundaries.

sections.title: What does a per-minute estimate cover?
paragraphs:
Use the written definition of a billable minute before estimating cost. Ask how rounding, unsuccessful attempts, transfers, hold time and test traffic are treated. The reviewed headline rate does not answer each of those questions.

For illustration only, 600 billable minutes at $0.16 would equal $96 in usage. That is arithmetic, not a total Callers quote. Add only confirmed number charges, taxes or other applicable items; do not invent fees to make the estimate appear complete. Likewise, do not omit a required Enterprise arrangement merely because Starter’s usage calculation looks attractive.

Callers’ pricing page describes standard US telephony, speech processing and models within its chosen-plan rate. Obtain the scope for your destinations and workflow rather than assuming that description includes every carrier arrangement or international call. [Callers.ai pricing](https://www.callers.ai/pricing/)

sections.title: Test the requirement that changes your package
paragraphs:
Use fictional caller details and obtain permission for a controlled demonstration. These are proposed checks, not tests performed on Callers here.

**If concurrency determines the plan:** agree on a small overlap within the test authorization. Observe each independent call and any transfer leg. Record the account configuration, observed result and documented treatment of the next caller. Do not flood a number to discover a limit.

**If your carrier determines the plan:** have the seller demonstrate the proposed route, not a different demo number. Record which party owns the number and which party changes the connection. Keep existing customer traffic unchanged until an authorized cutover is approved.

**If support determines the plan:** identify who handles a configuration problem. An AI help widget and a person assigned to implementation are different services. Confirm the escalation path before assuming either will complete the work for your office.

| Acceptance record | Fill after the authorized demonstration |
|---|---|
| Requirement and chosen package | ___ |

| Account configuration and demonstration date | ___ |
| Observed result | ___ |
| Unresolved issue and responsible person | ___ |

sections.title: Choose the eligible package before comparing total cost
paragraphs:
Callers may be worth evaluating when its documented voice-agent offer matches your phone route and your team can operate the selected arrangement. If a required feature belongs to Enterprise, compare the Enterprise proposal rather than using Starter as a proxy price.

For another AI answering option, [review Revo’s current plans](https://www.revoapp.ai/pricing.html) and confirm the exact supported phone and booking setup. This guide establishes no Revo SIP, concurrency, support or native integration equivalence with Callers.ai.

Do not turn “billing period” into “month” for a price comparison. A shorter recurring period would produce a different annual total, but the reviewed evidence does not establish that My Receptionist uses a particular shorter cycle. Leave the conversion open until the provider confirms it.

sections.title: Separate answering minutes from the broader service scope
paragraphs:
My Receptionist’s feature page describes online scheduling, appointment reminders and secure messaging, with pricing dependent on the scope. Its process page describes forwarding calls to the service, receptionist handling and delivery of information through selected channels. [Features and add-ons](https://myreceptionist.com/features/) and [how the service works](https://myreceptionist.com/how-it-works/)

Ask for an answering-only quote and a quote that includes the additional tasks you actually need. That does not mean those tasks necessarily carry separate fees. It means the proposal should explicitly state whether they are included, optional or outside scope.

For a cleaning or restoration office, the difference could be between recording a request for an estimate and managing an appointment in an authorized scheduling system. If your office only needs the first outcome, avoid assuming it needs a broader package. If it needs the second, do not rely on a message-taking feature list as proof of the complete workflow.

sections.title: Build a two-part quote record
paragraphs:
Use this original worksheet to preserve what the published offer establishes and what the seller still needs to answer.

| Part of the proposal | Published starting point | Written answer to obtain |
|---|---|---|
| Base package | Named plan, charge and minute allowance | Exact start/end dates of one billing period; renewal basis |
| Excess usage | Plan-dependent overage referenced | Rate, rounding and chargeable activities |
| Setup | Setup charge listed | What work it covers and whether proposed changes add charges |
| Scheduling | Described as an available service | Software, actor, allowed operations and inclusion or additional fee |
| Reminders | Described as an available service | Who initiates the reminder, channel, usage treatment and scope |
| Message delivery | Channels described in service material | Selected destination, access and any separately quoted service |

Write the quote date beside the answers. If a salesperson resolves a term verbally, request it in the proposal rather than carrying a remembered assumption into your budget.

### Keep the billing calendar explicit

Ask for the first service period, invoice date and next renewal date. Then compare providers over the same time horizon. Use the seller’s exact allowance reset rule; do not assume unused minutes roll forward.

A useful quote records base charges, usage and optional services separately. If the provider bundles them, retain the bundle description instead of counting the same service twice. Unknown charges should remain unknown, not silently become zero.

### Keep the appointment work explicit

Have the seller identify what happens when the caller asks to book, move or cancel an appointment. Request the system and role used for each action. A broad calendar-management claim is not evidence that your specific software permits those actions through the proposed account.

The purpose here is to establish what you are buying. Use the existing [appointment-booking guide](/ai-answering-service/appointment-booking) for your office’s booking rules rather than rebuilding those rules in the price quote.

sections.title: Demonstrate the added work before accepting the added scope
paragraphs:
Ask for an authorized demonstration using fictional customer `DEMO-MR-01`. First request basic answering and message delivery. Then ask for the proposed scheduling task. Record which part of the service changes and how the seller says each part is charged.

| Demonstration | Record to inspect | Commercial question | Observed result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Answer and deliver an estimate inquiry | Message and destination | Which handling time uses the allowance? | ___ |
| Perform the quoted scheduling action | Appointment or pending-request reference | Is this included in the package or separately scoped? | ___ |
| Send a quoted reminder, if required | Authorized reminder record | How are initiation, attempts and usage treated? | ___ |

intro: GoHighLevel AI receptionist pricing is not one all-inclusive number. A home-service business needs to identify the HighLevel account arrangement, the Voice AI plan and the telephone charges. If an agency supplies the account, its customer-facing package is another part of the comparison.

sections.title: Identify who supplies the account
paragraphs:
There are two purchasing arrangements to distinguish:

- **You operate an eligible HighLevel account.** Identify the platform subscription you already pay for—or would need—before adding AI and phone charges.
- **An agency supplies a HighLevel subaccount.** Read the agency's proposal to find which platform access, AI service, configuration and support are bundled, and which charges are separate.

HighLevel's pricing guide says an active subscription and account are required to use its additional services. It also describes agency-wallet funding for supported usage. The AI price alone is therefore not evidence that the underlying platform account is free. [HighLevel Pricing Guide](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000001156-highlevel-pricing-guide).

Do not add an agency's own platform subscription to your customer quote automatically. If the agency's package already includes the relevant access, counting it again would inflate the comparison. Conversely, an AI allowance does not establish that setup or ongoing support is included.

sections.title: Read the AI plan separately from the phone bill
paragraphs:
HighLevel's current pricing documentation lists these Voice AI arrangements:

| AI option | Documented monthly AI subscription | Voice AI treatment | What remains outside this headline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pay-Per-Use | No monthly AI subscription fee | Applicable usage charges | Base platform arrangement, Phone System charges and any separately quoted services |
| AI Employee Growth | $50 per enabled location | 100 minutes shared by inbound, outbound and widget Voice AI; additional usage at applicable rates | Phone System charges and other separately applicable costs |
| AI Employee Unlimited | $97 per enabled location | Supported Voice AI usage included, subject to fair use | Phone System charges and other separately applicable costs |

“Unlimited” does not mean that every phone call has a zero total cost. Use the selected product's current rate details and confirm the price shown in the actual account. [AI Employee plan and phone-charge distinctions](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003906-ai-employee-access-rebilling-and-reselling), cross-checked with [AI Product Pricing, modified October 20, 2026](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006652-ai-product).

Record what the enabled location represents in the proposed setup. Do not assume that every physical branch creates a separate subscription, or that several configured locations share an allowance, without checking the account arrangement.

sections.title: Do not turn one voice rate into an all-in call price
paragraphs:
The current Voice AI documentation distinguishes text-to-speech component pricing from speech-to-speech pricing. For the former, voice processing, the chosen speech model and language-model usage contribute to AI cost. The latter has documented bundled AI rates. Phone charges remain a separate consideration. Use the selected architecture's rate card, not a formula copied from another configuration. [Voice AI pricing details](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000006652-ai-product).

For the buyer, the useful question is: **Which exact charge would this call create in my proposed account?** Ask the supplier to show the selected model, the measured unit, applicable allowance and separately charged phone usage. A sample calculation that leaves out a component should be labeled a subtotal, not a total.

Keep historical and current rate sheets separate. An old tutorial or screenshot can explain what somebody paid at the time without establishing your current offer.

sections.title: Understand an agency quote without becoming a reseller
paragraphs:
HighLevel distinguishes **rebilling usage** from **reselling a recurring AI subscription**. An agency can therefore present a customer price that differs from HighLevel's underlying charge. Ask which arrangement your proposal uses, who supplies support and where you can review the usage that reaches your bill. [AI Employee access, rebilling and reselling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000003906-ai-employee-access-rebilling-and-reselling).

A fixed client-facing rate per minute is still a usage rate, not an unlimited flat monthly price. HighLevel's fixed-rate documentation separates that client rate from the agency's underlying costs. [Fixed-Rate Rebilling](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000008422-fixed-rate-rebilling-for-ai-products).

This is a buyer's reconciliation, not instructions to enable rebilling, change a customer's price or buy an agency upgrade. Have the account owner confirm the applicable arrangement in writing.

sections.title: Use the quote-reconciliation matrix
paragraphs:
Complete the [HighLevel quote worksheet](quote-reconciliation-worksheet.md) from the actual proposal. Mark unknowns as unresolved; do not substitute an industry average.

| Component | What to record | Check against the contractor's quote |
|---|---|---|
| Platform access | Account supplier, subscription scope and required access | Is it already bundled or separately payable? |
| AI subscription | Plan, enabled-location count and billing period | Is this the platform charge or the agency's customer price? |
| Additional AI usage | Unit, model/configuration, allowance and applicable rate | Which activity can create another charge? |
| Phone usage and numbers | Relevant phone-service scope and written charging terms | What remains payable even if AI usage is included? |
| Setup and support | Tasks, owner, one-time versus recurring amount | Who maintains the configuration and resolves problems? |
| Limits and authorization | Person who can view charges or approve more usage | What happens when the current allowance or chosen limit is reached? |

### Worked example: a shared usage allowance

Consider a fictional Growth location using **80 inbound minutes, 15 outbound minutes and 10 widget minutes** in one billing month. Under the documented shared allowance, that is **105 Voice AI minutes**, or **5 minutes above 100**. Counting only inbound calls would miss part of this example's usage.

This calculation identifies excess units, not their complete dollar charge. The selected configuration, applicable rates and phone activity are still required. The example does not authorize outbound calling or establish its permissions.

### Worked example: avoid counting a bundle twice

A fictional agency offers a **$180 monthly package** that expressly includes platform access and the selected AI subscription, while excluding phone charges. Those assumptions make $180 the known recurring package subtotal—not $180 plus another $50 AI subscription. The remaining telephone amount and any separately agreed usage or support charges still need to be resolved.

The $180 figure is invented solely to demonstrate the arithmetic. It is not a HighLevel or agency offer. If the real quote does not clearly include the AI subscription, do not assume this treatment applies.

For a business-operated account, the corresponding comparison starts with its actual platform arrangement plus the applicable AI and phone components. Do not force a total while a required component is unknown.

sections.title: Check the consequence of a usage limit
paragraphs:
A usage alert and a stop condition serve different purposes. HighLevel's usage-limit documentation describes both continued operation with notifications and blocking at a configured limit. Confirm which setting applies to the proposed subaccount, who can change it and what a caller-facing workflow does if AI pauses. This article does not verify actual account enforcement or establish a ceiling on the entire phone bill. [AI Usage Limits](https://help.gohighlevel.com/support/solutions/articles/155000007813-ai-usage-limits).

Do not assume that choosing the lowest limit is harmless. Your office still needs a defined way to receive and follow up on requests when the AI workflow cannot operate. Ask for an authorized demonstration before routing customers; do not deliberately interrupt a live account to find out.

sections.title: Decide from the complete configured scope
paragraphs:
Before accepting the offer, resolve these points:

1. Which HighLevel account and enabled location will provide the service?
2. Which components are included in the customer price, and which are separately metered?
3. Who owns configuration, support, charge review and additional-usage approval?
4. What will a representative authorized inquiry produce: a message, a pending request or a confirmed booking in the agreed destination?
5. What happens if the workflow pauses, the office cannot accept the request or a connection fails?

If your business already uses HighLevel, compare the incremental configured cost and remaining office work. If you only need call answering, compare a narrower answering service against the same required tasks—not against the price of an entire platform serving other purposes.

Use the existing [answering-service cost guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-cost) for the broader billing comparison and [receptionist selection guide](/ai-answering-service/choose-virtual-receptionist) for operating requirements. Revo's [published service](https://www.revoapp.ai/services.html) is a separate option to evaluate; this page does not claim a Revo–HighLevel integration or that either product is universally cheaper.

takeaway: Decide from the complete configured scope

title: Lower answering service cost: reconcile the bill first
description: Match answering-service charges to agreed billing rules and compare cost changes without cutting required coverage.
lead: To lower an answering-service bill, first establish what the bill represents. A busier period, different billing rules, an additional task or a one-time charge can explain an increase. An amount you cannot yet explain is a question to investigate—not proof that the provider overcharged you.
intro: To lower an answering-service bill, first establish what the bill represents. A busier period, different billing rules, an additional task or a one-time charge can explain an increase. An amount you cannot yet explain is a question to investigate—not proof that the provider overcharged you.

sections.title: 1. Put the invoice and its rules in the same period
paragraphs:
Gather the invoice, the applicable rate sheet or agreement, approved changes and the activity records your business is authorized to inspect. Record the start and end dates and the time zone. Do not assume the invoice issue date is the beginning of its usage period.

Write down the billing unit, included allowance, reset rule, excess-usage rate and rounding method. If the terms round each activity separately, adding raw seconds and rounding the monthly total will produce a different calculation. If the unit is calls or distinct customers, a minute calculation is not a substitute.

Keep missing information visible. A blank rate is not zero. An incomplete export cannot establish the complete period's usage. If a term or charge is unclear, record the exact question for the provider rather than filling the gap with another provider's rules.

The [service agreement checklist](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/answering-service-contract-checklist) helps locate the documents and responsible people. This ledger connects those documents to individual charges. Use anonymized activity references; copying customer names or complete recordings into a cost worksheet is usually unnecessary.

sections.title: 2. Reconcile chargeable activity, not just conversation length
paragraphs:
For each invoice category, identify the supporting activity and the agreed rule. The relevant evidence might be a call record, transfer attempt or other recorded work if the contract makes it chargeable. Do not assume either that such work is always billed or that it is always included.

Keep operational workload separate from billing. [Average handle time](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/average-handle-time) measures a defined handling process. The provider's contractual usage unit may include different events, exclusions or rounding. A mismatch between those totals is not, by itself, a billing error.

The fictional audit uses a calendar-month plan with a $40 recurring fee, 10 included billable minutes and $2 per additional minute. Its invented rules round each eligible activity up to the next 30 seconds, sum those rounded activities, and apply the allowance once to that sum. Partial additional minutes are charged proportionally. The model has no separate transfer surcharge or minimum beyond that rounding rule.

Eight available activity records contain 677 raw seconds. Rounding each one as specified produces 810 seconds, or **13.5 billable minutes**. Rounding the combined raw time only once would produce 11.5 minutes; that is not this fictional contract's method.

sections.title: 3. Leave an unexplained difference unresolved
paragraphs:
The fictional invoice states 15 billable minutes. Its arithmetic follows the stated quantity: five excess minutes at $2 produce a $10 usage charge. The eight available records support only 3.5 excess minutes and $7 of usage charges. The export has not been confirmed complete.

| Fictional charge | Invoice amount | Amount supported by available evidence | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Monthly base | $40 | $40 | Matches the fictional rate sheet |
| Excess usage | $10 | $7 | $3 difference; 1.5 billed minutes lack supporting records |
| Optional recurring report add-on | $8 | $8 | Matches the fictional authorization |
| One-time setup | $12 | $12 | Matches the fictional authorization |
| One-time credit | −$5 | −$5 | Matches the fictional credit note |
| **Pretax subtotal** | **$65** | **$62** | **$3 unexplained; not a proven overcharge** |

The $62 column is **not a corrected bill or the established amount owed**. Additional eligible activity could explain the difference. Ask for the records behind the unmatched usage and the rule applied to them. If evidence establishes an error, request the provider's correction process; if it establishes valid activity, update the reconciliation. Until then, keep the issue open.

An auditable question is more useful than a vague complaint: “Please identify the activity supporting the remaining 1.5 billable minutes in this period, including the duration and rounding applied.” The worksheet keeps that request, its owner and the response together.

sections.title: 4. Separate recurring cost from a temporarily smaller invoice
paragraphs:
Do not count a one-time credit as a recurring reduction. Equally, the disappearance of a setup fee can lower a later invoice even though the plan and usage cost have not improved.

## 2. Reconcile chargeable activity, not just conversation length

For each invoice category, identify the supporting activity and the agreed rule. The relevant evidence might be a call record, transfer attempt or other recorded work if the contract makes it chargeable. Do not assume either that such work is always billed or that it is always included.

Keep operational workload separate from billing. [Average handle time](https://www.revoapp.ai/ai-answering-service/average-handle-time) measures a defined handling process. The provider's contractual usage unit may include different events, exclusions or rounding. A mismatch between those totals is not, by itself, a billing error.

The fictional audit uses a calendar-month plan with a $40 recurring fee, 10 included billable minutes and $2 per additional minute. Its invented rules round each eligible activity up to the next 30 seconds, sum those rounded activities, and apply the allowance once to that sum. Partial additional minutes are charged proportionally. The model has no separate transfer surcharge or minimum beyond that rounding rule.

Eight available activity records contain 677 raw seconds. Rounding each one as specified produces 810 seconds, or **13.5 billable minutes**. Rounding the combined raw time only once would produce 11.5 minutes; that is not this fictional contract's method.

title: Workiz Genius Answering: transfers and the fallback
description: Compare Workiz Genius Answering with a separate answering service by transfer control, record boundaries and unavailable-team handling.
lead: For a service business already using Workiz, choosing AI answering means choosing where the conversation and its records live. Genius Answering is built into Workiz. A separate answering service may use a different phone path and handoff. Compare the point where a person takes over, especially when the requested team member cannot answer.
intro: For a service business already using Workiz, choosing AI answering means choosing where the conversation and its records live. Genius Answering is built into Workiz. A separate answering service may use a different phone path and handoff. Compare the point where a person takes over, especially when the requested team member cannot answer.

sections.title: Start with the Workiz workflow you want to retain
paragraphs: Workiz describes Genius Answering as an embedded product that can handle calls and booking tasks. Its settings documentation says new appointments can be saved as jobs or leads. Before comparing it with another provider, decide which result your office requires. A lead awaiting review and an accepted job are different outcomes.

Ask Workiz to demonstrate the proposed configuration with a fictional service request. Record where the customer, service location and requested work appear. If you want to retain Workiz as your operating system, compare the complete office handoff rather than only how natural the opening conversation sounds.

sections.title: Compare validated and automatic transfers
paragraphs: Workiz documents an optional validation step before transferring. With validation enabled, the receiving person hears the request and can accept or decline. Without it, the requested person is connected automatically when they answer, without that briefing. Confirm the setting in the proposed account rather than assuming every transfer is attended.

Use three fictional calls in the demonstration: a request for the owner, a request for a named employee and a general request for a person. Decide which recipients should be offered each call. A transfer rule must not imply that the owner or a technician is always available.

sections.title: Inspect what happens after an external transfer
paragraphs: Workiz warns that a call transferred to an external number cannot reenter its original flow. It says transcription is available up to the transfer, while an unanswered external call can reach that number’s voicemail. A call log is therefore not proof that the office retains the complete later conversation or voicemail.

This is the most useful exception test for an owner whose destination is a personal mobile. Arrange an authorized test where that recipient does not answer. Inspect the caller’s experience and where the unresolved message can be accessed. Do not accept a successful ringing test as evidence of a working no-answer process.

Write an original handoff card with five fields: reason for involving a person; requested destination; whether acceptance is required; record available after transfer; and owner of an unanswered request. Fill observed outcomes only after the demonstration.

sections.title: Compare a separate answering service on the same boundary
paragraphs: If Revo is on your shortlist, ask it to demonstrate the exact answering, booking and transfer actions available in your proposed plan. Its general field-service connection label does not establish a Workiz integration, a particular transfer mode or continued recording after the handoff. Leave those requirements unresolved until confirmed.

Compare three deliverables in each proposal: the request or job record, the person receiving an exception and the no-answer outcome. Also obtain the relevant phone prerequisites, usage unit and service terms directly. This guide does not reproduce an unverified price or claim one provider produces better results.

Use the existing Revo Services and Pricing pages to scope the answering offer. Choose the setup whose demonstrated handoff matches the way your office works; keep software migration and customer-call routing as separate decisions.

faqs.q: Does this guide establish that Revo integrates with Workiz?
faqs.a: No. Confirm the named platform, supported actions and plan directly. A general integration feature is insufficient evidence.

faqs.q: Is an external transfer the same as keeping the caller in Workiz?
faqs.a: Workiz documents a record boundary when a call leaves its flow. Test the destination and no-answer outcome before relying on it.

takeaway: Review the proposed answering workflow against your own operating rules before routing customer calls.

title: FieldEdge answering: a lead or a confirmed booking?
description: Evaluate FieldEdge answering by the record actually created. Separate a lead awaiting CSR confirmation from a confirmed appointment.
lead: A FieldEdge answering service can capture an inquiry without creating the appointment your customer thinks was booked. Before choosing a provider, establish the exact record it creates, who confirms the visit and what the caller hears while that confirmation remains pending. The word integration does not answer those questions.
intro: A FieldEdge answering service can capture an inquiry without creating the appointment your customer thinks was booked. Before choosing a provider, establish the exact record it creates, who confirms the visit and what the caller hears while that confirmation remains pending. The word integration does not answer those questions.

sections.title: Resolve the difference in published descriptions
paragraphs: FieldEdge’s September 15, 2026 announcement describes a direct Free2Grow integration and automatic appointment booking. Free2Grow’s more specific FieldEdge page describes recognizing returning callers, collecting request details and creating a lead for CSRs to confirm. It also describes seeing later lead-to-job or quote changes.

Those descriptions do not establish one universal behavior for every account. Ask both companies which workflow applies to your proposed configuration today. Treat the difference as an unresolved scope question, not proof of a malfunction or a reason to silently pick the more expansive claim.

sections.title: Decide what a caller may be told
paragraphs: Your office should write two approved outcomes. For a lead-only path, the message can say the request is awaiting office confirmation. For a supported booking path, confirmation requires the authoritative appointment or job to exist with the correct customer, location and time.

Ask the provider to show the created record during a demonstration. Read the type and status rather than relying on a calendar-shaped screen or a verbal assurance. If staff must review availability before converting the lead, include that work in the proposal’s operating scope.

sections.title: Use a lead-to-job evidence card
paragraphs: Fictional case: an existing customer calls about a repair at a second property. Record the caller match, selected service address, request reference, created record type, assigned CSR and next action. Then ask the authorized CSR to accept or decline the request through the proposed workflow.

Inspect what the answering system learns after the change. If the lead becomes a quote rather than a job, check that no appointment confirmation is sent. If the office declines the request, identify who tells the customer and which pending work remains. Do not infer this from a general claim about synchronization.

Keep a simple state ledger: request received; lead created; office decision pending; accepted job or quote; customer informed; exception owner. These are proposed review states, not documented FieldEdge API statuses. A record that cannot be reconciled stays pending for its owner.

sections.title: Compare direct integration with an office handoff
paragraphs: A separate answering service can still be useful when your office wants approved intake and a clear callback request. Compare that actual scope with direct software actions rather than calling every path an integration. The important purchasing question is which work the office retains.

Revo’s Services and Pricing pages describe its general answering offer and plan boundaries. This article does not establish a Revo–FieldEdge connector. Ask Revo whether the proposed setup captures a request, writes a particular record or supports confirmed booking; require the corresponding evidence.

Use the same fictional second-property request for every finalist. Select only after the record, customer wording and remaining CSR work agree. Do not compare prices as if lead capture and completed booking were identical services.

faqs.q: Does direct integration always mean automatic booking?
faqs.a: No. Confirm the record type, confirmation responsibility and current configuration. The reviewed FieldEdge and Free2Grow descriptions differ in scope.

faqs.q: Can a lead be described as a confirmed appointment?
faqs.a: Only when the separate booking action has actually completed and its details have been verified. A lead awaiting CSR review should remain a request.

takeaway: Review the proposed answering workflow against your own operating rules before routing customer calls.

title: FieldPulse Operator AI: phone and chat ownership
description: Compare FieldPulse Operator AI, Chat AI and separate answering by channel, booking responsibility and requests that cross from chat to phone.
lead: A FieldPulse business choosing customer-response tools needs to separate the incoming phone conversation from website chat. Operator AI and Chat AI are different parts of FieldPulse’s offer. Decide which channel needs coverage, which system owns the resulting job and who handles a request that moves between channels.
intro: A FieldPulse business choosing customer-response tools needs to separate the incoming phone conversation from website chat. Operator AI and Chat AI are different parts of FieldPulse’s offer. Decide which channel needs coverage, which system owns the resulting job and who handles a request that moves between channels.

sections.title: Separate phone answering from website chat
paragraphs: FieldPulse describes Operator AI as its phone agent for inbound calls, with booking inside FieldPulse. Its Field Intelligence and Chat AI pages separately describe the website conversation product. Confirm which products are enabled in the proposed account.

A buyer should therefore ask which product is included in the proposed package. Do not treat a website chatbot demonstration as proof that phone calls are covered, or assume phone answering automatically includes chat. Obtain the channel, account and enabled capabilities in writing.

sections.title: Give one request one accountable owner
paragraphs: Fictional case: a homeowner starts a web chat, then calls because they need to explain the request. Before testing any product, decide how staff will identify whether those interactions concern the same customer, property and requested work. A matching first name alone is insufficient.

Ask the provider to demonstrate the proposed cross-channel path. Inspect the customer and job records after the chat and after the call. If the flow creates two requests, identify who reconciles them. If the caller changes the service address, ensure the change is reviewed rather than silently applied to an unrelated record.

sections.title: Test three different outcomes
paragraphs: First, test a supported service at a time the actual configuration can book. Inspect the resulting job and the customer wording. Second, request a service the company does not offer. The expected result should follow your approved exclusion, not invent a new service to complete the booking.

Third, move from a chat to a call about an existing request. Record the original reference, later interaction, resulting job count and next owner. These are proposed acceptance cases, not tests already run against FieldPulse.

Keep the outcome ledger short: channel received; request identified; permitted action; resulting record; customer told; unresolved owner. A chat-to-phone transition is not proof of a successful job creation. Confirm each event separately in the actual account.

sections.title: Compare an independent answering option fairly
paragraphs: If the need is phone coverage while your office retains scheduling control, ask a separate answering provider to demonstrate that narrower handoff. If the need is native FieldPulse booking across phone and chat, ask FieldPulse to show the exact workflow and inclusions. The two proposals may leave different work with your team.

Revo should be evaluated against its published answering plans and a verified proposed setup. This article does not claim a Revo–FieldPulse integration, native Chat AI service or automatic reconciliation of cross-channel requests. Do not assume those capabilities from a general software-connection label.

Use Revo’s existing Services and Pricing pages for the commercial starting point. Choose by the channels and records your office actually needs, with exceptions assigned before customer calls are routed.

faqs.q: Is Operator AI the same product as Chat AI?
faqs.a: FieldPulse documents them separately for phone and website-chat interactions. Confirm the exact enabled products and package with FieldPulse.

faqs.q: Does this comparison prove that Revo writes jobs into FieldPulse?
faqs.a: No. A named connection and its supported actions require separate verification in the proposed setup.

takeaway: Review the proposed answering workflow against your own operating rules before routing customer calls.

title: Dispatch fee phone script: explain the visit charge
description: Write a dispatch-fee script that separates the visit charge from repair pricing and preserves approved credits, waivers and exceptions.
lead: When a homeowner asks what a service visit costs, the receptionist needs your approved fee policy before offering a time. A dispatch or diagnostic charge may differ from the repair price. Explain what the stated charge covers, whether any credit applies and which questions need an authorized employee. This guide supplies original wording, not a recommended fee.
intro: When a homeowner asks what a service visit costs, the receptionist needs your approved fee policy before offering a time. A dispatch or diagnostic charge may differ from the repair price. Explain what the stated charge covers, whether any credit applies and which questions need an authorized employee. This guide supplies original wording, not a recommended fee.

sections.title: Prepare a fee card before writing the script
paragraphs: For each applicable service type, record the approved charge, what it covers, whether it changes by time or location, and any documented credit or waiver. Identify who maintains the policy and its effective date. An unanswered field should send the request to review; it should not be filled from another contractor’s price.

ServiceTitan’s Voice Agent release documentation describes customizable dispatch-fee messages tied to job types. It illustrates why a general fee sentence may be insufficient. That is evidence about ServiceTitan’s feature, not proof that Revo offers the same configuration controls.

sections.title: Use wording that matches the approved policy
paragraphs: Standard visit: “For [approved service type], the [visit or diagnostic] charge is [approved amount]. It covers [approved scope]. Repair work is [your approved explanation of separate quoting]. Would you like me to explain the next booking step?”

Credit toward work: “Your visit charge is [approved amount]. Under our current policy, [precise credit condition]. The team will explain and obtain approval for any separate repair work.” Use this only when the credit condition is current and applies to the request.

Unverified exception: “I do not want to give you an incorrect charge. I can record your question for [authorized role] to confirm before the visit is accepted.” These are original templates. Bracketed fields are instructions for the business to replace, never words to publish in a live script.

sections.title: Keep three different objections separate
paragraphs: “Is that the total repair price?” calls for the approved distinction between the visit and later work. It does not authorize the receptionist to diagnose the fault or invent a repair estimate. “Does my membership waive it?” requires the business’s actual eligibility check. “The last person quoted something else” requires a review of the earlier statement.

Build one fictional case for each objection. Give the evaluator an approved fee card and expected escalation owner. The script passes only when it states the applicable policy without adding a guarantee. A polite conversation that promises an unverified waiver fails the test.

Also test a request outside the fee card’s scope. For example, a business may have different rules for an estimate visit and a repair diagnostic. The correct result can be an office review rather than a quoted amount.

sections.title: Choose answering around policy control
paragraphs: When evaluating a receptionist, ask how approved wording is maintained, who can change it and what happens when the policy does not answer the caller’s question. Test a current rule, a changed rule and an excluded request. Keep the dated fee card as the comparison input for every provider.

Revo’s published offer includes your own script and rules, subject to the selected plan and supported setup. Confirm how the proposed configuration handles fee information and exceptions. This article does not promise dynamic pricebook access, membership verification, payment collection or repair quoting.

Use the existing Revo Services and Pricing pages to scope the offer. The buying decision is whether the answering process can explain your policy accurately and hand uncertainty back to the office before an unsupported promise is made.

faqs.q: What amount should a contractor charge?
faqs.a: This guide does not recommend an amount. Use the business’s approved fee policy and quote process.

faqs.q: Does a fee script confirm the repair price?
faqs.a: No. State the approved scope of the visit charge and keep any separate repair proposal under the business’s actual authorization process.

title: Recurring cleaning calls: change a visit or the series
description: Design cleaning-call intake for one skipped visit, a series change or a crew request without silently changing future appointments.
lead: “Skip next week” and “stop future cleanings” describe different requests. A cleaning business choosing answering and scheduling support needs to preserve that difference. intro: “Skip next week” and “stop future cleanings” describe different requests. A cleaning business choosing answering and scheduling support needs to preserve that difference. Define whether the caller wants to change one visit, the future series or the assigned team, then confirm only the action your actual setup can complete.

sections.title: Ask which part of the schedule should change
paragraphs: Begin with the existing customer and service address through the business’s approved identification process. Ask for the affected date, then clarify whether the request concerns that occurrence only or future visits as well. Do not assume a one-time skip cancels the continuing service.

Jobber’s documentation distinguishes jobs from visits and describes visit-specific edits separately from changes that update future visits. That makes it a useful example of why the object being changed matters. It does not establish that every cleaning platform uses the same controls or that Revo connects to Jobber.

sections.title: Use a three-case call card
paragraphs: One occurrence: “Do you want to skip [date] only and keep the later visits unchanged?” Record the stated scope and proposed next step. If your system cannot verify the later visits, leave the change for the scheduling owner rather than claiming they remain intact.

Future series: “From which date should the new frequency or schedule begin?” Capture the effective date and requested cadence. An open slot next Tuesday does not establish capacity for every future Tuesday.

Crew preference: “Is this a request about the team for one visit or for future service?” Record the preference without promising a named employee. Availability, staffing and assignment remain with the person authorized to manage the cleaning team.

sections.title: Inspect the affected and unaffected records
paragraphs: Fictional example: visits are planned for November 3, 10 and 17. The customer asks to skip November 10 only. The acceptance check should inspect November 10 and also confirm the intended states of November 3 and 17. Those invented dates illustrate scope, not an actual customer schedule.

A series-change test needs a different expected result. If the customer requests a new cadence beginning November 10, write the intended future schedule before the demonstration. Review which visits changed and whether pending reminders still match the result. Refer to the system’s documented reminder behavior; do not assume it updates automatically.

Keep a change ledger with the request reference, original visit or series reference, scope, effective date, expected affected records, observed result and unresolved owner. Do not put customer access codes or unnecessary private details into a review worksheet.

sections.title: Compare capture-only with supported schedule changes
paragraphs: Some answering arrangements collect the change for an office scheduler. Others may perform specified actions in a supported destination. Compare those scopes honestly. A clear request with a named owner can be appropriate when the office wants to retain control over future capacity.

Revo’s published cleaning-answering guide already distinguishes recurring and one-time work. This page adds a series-scope acceptance task for choosing the supported workflow. It does not establish native recurring-job editing, crew assignment or a connection to any named cleaning platform.

Review the proposed setup through Revo’s existing Services and Pricing pages. Before allowing confirmations, test one skipped visit, one future-series change and one unavailable crew preference against your own policy.

faqs.q: Does skipping a visit cancel the recurring service?
faqs.a: Not unless that is the customer’s verified request and the business’s supported action. Preserve the requested scope explicitly.

faqs.q: Can the receptionist promise the usual cleaning team?
faqs.a: Only if the actual staffing workflow authorizes and verifies that commitment. Otherwise capture a preference for the scheduler.

sections.title: Separate four reasons for calling
paragraphs: Use a short request taxonomy: a new damage inquiry; a question about an existing project; a request to change a planned visit; or a question about a document or charge. The business should approve the responsible role for each. Do not route every call containing a damage description as a new loss.

Avoca has a restoration-specific AI CSR page, while restoration software vendors describe project and field-documentation tools. Those are different product categories. A communications feature does not establish that an answering system can read every project record or explain an insurer’s decision. Ask the proposed provider which records and actions are actually available.

sections.title: Choose capture-only or verified record access
paragraphs: In a capture-only arrangement, the receptionist records the project reference supplied by the caller, the service location, the question and the callback details needed by the owner. The response should accurately say the team must review the question. It must not turn the caller’s statement into an official job status.

If a provider proposes reading project information, ask which field is authoritative, when it was updated, who may receive it and which questions still require staff. A note about yesterday’s plan is not proof that a crew will arrive today. The office must approve the permitted explanation and access boundaries.

sections.title: Track a request through ownership and response
paragraphs: Use an original request ledger with six fields: request reference; existing project reference; caller’s stated question; responsible role; office review deadline or policy; and evidence that the response was completed. Leave the last field blank until the authorized person actually responds.

Fictional test A: a property owner asks when a worker will return. Test whether the request reaches the designated project role without an invented arrival time. Test B: a caller disputes a project status already mentioned by someone else. Keep the discrepancy visible for review rather than choosing whichever statement sounds more plausible.

Test C: the normal project contact is unavailable. Check the approved backup and how the office recognizes the unresolved request. The call should not disappear merely because a transfer attempt occurred. These are proposed evaluations, not measured provider results or a guaranteed response schedule.

sections.title: Keep the Revo buying decision inside the answering scope
paragraphs: The existing after-hours restoration page covers first-call information and a permitted next step. This guide focuses on the ongoing project-question queue: ownership, unanswered requests and evidence of a later response. It is not a project-management software comparison or an instruction to assess damage over the phone.

Revo’s published answering, scripts and summaries can be considered within a confirmed proposed setup. Ask what the office receives, which transfer options the selected plan supports and who owns follow-up. This page does not claim Revo reads restoration project systems, updates claims, verifies coverage, controls crews or supplies live field status.

Use the existing Services and Pricing pages to scope that offer. Choose an answering arrangement that keeps project questions visible to their owners; evaluate any additional project-record access as a separate, evidenced requirement.

faqs.q: Can an answering service confirm a crew arrival from a call message?
faqs.a: A call message alone is insufficient. Confirm arrival information through the business’s authoritative scheduling or field process.

faqs.q: Is this another new-loss intake page?
faqs.a: No. It evaluates how questions about work already underway are assigned, tracked and answered by the responsible office role.

sections.title: Define the inquiry you want before choosing a channel
paragraphs: Write a one-sentence offer: the service, the area served and the next step a prospective customer can request. A maintenance inquiry, a replacement consultation and an urgent repair request need different capacity and follow-up. Keep work you cannot accept outside the promoted offer.

Create an original channel card with these fields: service; customer type; service area; available next step; channel; contact destination; owner; and review date. If the office cannot explain what happens after the customer calls, finish that part before increasing promotion.

sections.title: Compare three sources of demand
paragraphs: Search visibility can help people already looking for a service find your business. Keep service descriptions and contact information consistent. Paid search is a separate decision about budget, targeting and measurement. This guide does not recommend a spend or start a campaign.

Referrals and local relationships can introduce people who know little about your company. Give partners an accurate service description and the normal contact route. Existing-customer inquiries may concern new work or an open job; identify which before treating them as new acquisition. Do not count every returning caller as a new lead.

sections.title: Keep one inquiry ledger across channels
paragraphs: Use one row per new inquiry with a stable reference, date, reported source, requested service, area, contact outcome and next owner. Preserve unknown source as unknown. A customer mentioning search does not by itself identify a particular ad or listing.

Fictional example: three calls about one replacement request remain one inquiry and three contacts. If a customer also asks about an unrelated repair at another property, the office may create a separate inquiry under its written rule. Define that rule before comparing channels.

Review qualified inquiries, appointments actually confirmed and later jobs separately. A qualified inquiry is not a completed job. Compare like periods and note whether the office had capacity to accept work. A change in jobs does not prove one marketing channel caused it.

sections.title: Use answering as the receiving step
paragraphs: A useful reception process captures what the caller wants and gives an accurate next step. It does not create demand by itself. Review missed requests and incomplete handoffs alongside acquisition activity so the owner can see whether the problem is reach, fit or office capacity.

Revo can be evaluated for its published answering scope through the Services and Pricing pages. Confirm the proposed intake and follow-up handoff. This guide does not claim Revo manages campaigns, attributes all leads or guarantees new HVAC customers.

faqs.a: No. Choose around the work, area, capacity and resources of the actual business.

faqs.q: Can I count calls as leads?
faqs.a: Keep contacts and distinct inquiries separate. Label the counting rule and retain repeat contacts without inflating new demand.

intro: Customer service survey questions should tell a home-service business what to improve. Keep the experience being rated clear: arranging service, speaking with the office and receiving the visit are different moments. A short question about the right moment is more useful than a long form with an ambiguous overall score.

sections.title: Choose one experience and one respondent
paragraphs: For an office-contact survey, identify the contact being discussed without exposing unnecessary customer details. For a post-visit survey, identify the completed visit. Do not ask someone to rate work that has not happened. Decide whether the respondent arranged the service, received it or both.

Use the business’s existing approved process for invitations and contact preferences. This guide is a questionnaire resource, not a request to send messages or enable an automated survey. Keep a route for a customer who needs help now rather than directing an unresolved issue only into a survey.

sections.title: Copy a short office-contact questionnaire
paragraphs: Original questions: 1. Was it clear what would happen after your contact with our office? Choose yes, partly, no or not applicable. 2. How easy or difficult was it to explain your request? Use a labeled scale from very easy to very difficult. 3. Were you asked to repeat information you had already provided about this request? Choose yes, no or unsure.

4. Was any information about your appointment unclear? Leave space to describe it without asking for payment details or access codes. 5. What one thing could make contacting us easier? Add an optional route for a follow-up request, making clear who reviews it. These are original sample questions, not a validated research instrument.

sections.title: Keep visit feedback in a separate block
paragraphs: For a completed visit, ask whether the customer understood the work discussed and the next step. Ask about arrival communication only when relevant. Include not applicable rather than forcing a rating for a step that did not occur. Do not combine the technician’s work quality with phone experience in one question.

Avoid leading wording such as “How excellent was our quick response?” Ask about one thing at a time. Test the draft with fictional scenarios: an inquiry with no booking, a booked future visit and a completed visit. Each person should see questions they can answer.

sections.title: Review counts before drawing conclusions
paragraphs: Report how many invitations were eligible under your process, how many people responded and which experience they rated. An unanswered invitation is not a positive or negative response. Do not generalize a handful of replies to every customer. Keep different scales separate.

Assign recurring themes to a responsible person and record the change made. A caller’s view of clarity can reveal a gap that an internal call-review rubric misses. Revo’s answering offer can be assessed separately through Services and Pricing; this guide does not establish a built-in survey tool or a satisfaction improvement guarantee.

faqs.q: Is this the same as reviewing call recordings?
faqs.a: No. The customer reports their experience; an internal review examines evidence of how the interaction was handled. Both have different limits.

faqs.q: Should I use a score or open comments?
faqs.a: Use a clearly labeled response scale for a specific question and an optional comment. Retain counts and context rather than reporting an unexplained average.
